p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / privacy-preserving inference / selective FHE
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that encrypting only sensitive ROIs can preserve exact outputs while locality-preserving architectures obtain order-of-magnitude homomorphic-evaluation speedups, whereas early global mixing removes the benefit. This is valuable architectural efficiency evidence, but the abstract presents conditional rather than a single deployment-wide benchmark, so it is retained as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Proxy Policy Steering
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / inference-time adaptation / flow policy steering
p1_watchlist.why: Inference-time adaptation trains lightweight reference and task proxy policies whose velocity-space residual steers a frozen generalist sampler at every denoising step. Across 8 real and 4 simulation manipulation tasks it improves pi-0.5 by 53% absolute success on average while retaining broad base capabilities; strong Physical-AI relevance, but no measured serving latency/compute reduction in the primary abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: DeCAL: Towards Physically-Grounded Dexterous Vision-Language-Action Models via Contact-Aware Latent Co-Imagination
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / dexterous manipulation / tactile fusion / world modeling
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI candidate. DeCAL combines specialized MoT experts, adaptive visuo-tactile fusion, and latent co-imagination for contact-rich dexterous manipulation, reaching 71% average success and 83.4% progress success. The current primary abstract does not report serving latency, throughput, memory, or a comparative runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: MeClear: Cooperative Game-Theoretic Attribution and Risk-Aware Memory Clearance for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent memory / context management
p1_watchlist.why: Task-conditioned memory clearance uses LOO screening plus sampled cooperative Shapley attribution to suppress harmful memories without modifying the persistent store. Across ten long-dialogue memory pools it reaches 85.9% target recall and 82.3% task recovery, +25.5 points over LOO, but no direct token/latency reduction is reported, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Ozaki 2.5: Engineering the Deconstruction Path of fp64-Emulated Dense Matrix Multiplication on FP8 Tensor Cores
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / FP8 tensor cores / mixed precision / GEMM / architecture co-design
p1_watchlist.why: High-value mixed-precision architecture/kernel work on FP64-emulated GEMM over FP8 tensor cores, including residue conversion, pipelining and a proposed stream-side conversion mechanism. The paper explicitly states that every performance result is a model projection pending measurement, so projected 235-473 TFLOPS and 1.6-1.9x gains are not promoted as measured systems evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: It's Not RoPE that Creates Sinks: The Role of Self-Concentration and Value-Non-Mixing in Attention
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / attention / massive activations / low-bit robustness
p1_watchlist.why: Mechanistic analysis directly relevant to low-bit quantization: it attributes attention sinks and massive activations to causal-mask-induced self-concentration and value non-mixing rather than RoPE. It may inform future quantization strategies, but it proposes no quantizer and reports no measured inference efficiency benefit, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Omni Interaction Agent Technical Report
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / efficient reasoning/agent systems / streaming full-duplex runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Gander is directly relevant to realtime multimodal agent infrastructure: a Cerebellum-Brain split, streaming Thinker-Talker, chunk-level ordered token stream, tool calling and an agent orchestration runtime support continuous full-duplex video/speech/text interaction and interruption. The primary report does not give hard end-to-end latency/throughput numbers for the orchestration design, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: GraphFAS: A Distributed System for Automated Graph Feature Generation and Selection in Industrial Transaction Networks
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / industrial graph systems / feature pipeline / production deployment
p1_watchlist.why: Production distributed graph-feature system deployed at Alipay, with explicit graph feature generation and distributed Boruta-style selection and reported order-of-magnitude engineering-efficiency improvement. This is useful production infrastructure evidence, but the abstract lacks a concrete throughput/latency/speedup baseline, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: SkillAdam: Stable and Efficient Skill Evolution for Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / skill optimization / agent memory / cost reduction
p1_watchlist.why: Relevant efficient-agent work: optimization memory stabilizes discrete skill updates and a volatility-driven edit budget adapts revision scope; across seven benchmarks it reports stronger skills with substantially fewer optimization iterations and lower cost than prior methods. Because the primary abstract gives no concrete wall-clock/token/cost reduction numbers, it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: DiffLUT-Net: Differentiable Training of FPGA LUT Networks with Learnable Connectivity
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI / FPGA / hardware-native networks
p1_watchlist.why: FPGA-native networks jointly learn six-input LUT truth tables and sparse connectivity, then export directly to synthesizable Verilog and prune unused logic. It reports favorable accuracy-resource tradeoffs across five benchmarks and releases code, but the abstract provides no exact latency/energy/throughput advantage, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Closing the Consistency Gap: Self-Evolving Agents That Learn to Stay on Course
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / episodic memory / production consistency
p1_watchlist.why: Converts unstable agent trajectory steps into episodic guidelines. On AppWorld with ReAct/GPT-4.1, all-five-runs success improves by +16 points same-task and +13 points similar-task. High-value agent-runtime reliability work, but not direct inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: Hi-FLoop: Hierarchical State-Feedback Loops for Multi-Timescale World Modeling
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / world models / multi-timescale closed-loop generation
p1_watchlist.why: Hierarchical branch-consistent traffic world model separates 8-s Goal, 2-s Preview, 1-s Control, and 0.5-s feedback commits, with sparse future interaction graphs and generated-state recovery. It directly matches multi-timescale Physical-AI system structure, but currently reports predictive quality rather than serving/runtime savings, so it remains protected watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Tools-CC-Bench: a Benchmark Suite for Collective Communication with Compression in HPC and AI Workloads
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / collective communication / compression / systems benchmarking
p1_watchlist.why: 7d replay recovered an application-oriented benchmark for compression-enabled collectives across realistic HPC and LLM workloads. CC-Bench profiles per-phase latency, hardware utilization, fidelity and computation interference across CPU/GPU clusters and multiple communication libraries. It is highly relevant infrastructure for communication-compression evaluation, but the abstract primarily contributes methodology and characterization rather than a new universally faster runtime, so it is retained as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Hyperparameter Scaling Laws Across MoE Sparsity
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / sparse training / scaling laws
p1_watchlist.why: The work runs 1,800 pre-training experiments spanning six activated-parameter scales, about 20T tokens and 200k H800-equivalent GPU-hours, deriving scaling laws that explicitly include activation ratio and validating on a 12B ultra-sparse MoE with 1/64 experts active. It is important MoE efficiency methodology but does not introduce a measured systems/runtime speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: BIFTA: Brain-Inspired Few-Shot Tactile Adaptation for Unknown Sensors
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / tactile sensing / few-shot adaptation / heterogeneous sensors
p1_watchlist.why: Adapts a frozen tactile encoder to previously unseen sensor hardware using a small labeled support set, dual-view statistical memory, spectral graphs, and uncertainty-gated propagation. With 10% labeled target data on SITR, mean Sparsh accuracy rises from 6.86% to 87.09%, but this is data-efficient adaptation rather than measured inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: MoEMB: Scaling Universal Multimodal Embeddings with Efficient Mixture-of-Experts Models
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / MoE systems / retrieval embeddings
p1_watchlist.why: MoEMB scales universal multimodal embeddings along the expert axis and studies adaptive computation. With only 3B active parameters it surpasses reasoning-token embedding methods using over 4x active parameters, but the current abstract emphasizes active compute and quality rather than measured serving latency or throughput, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: CoordFormer: Give Me Any Coordinates and I Will Give You Labels
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / high-resolution inference / edge-cloud vision
p1_watchlist.why: Coordinate decoding with localized cross-attention combines downsampled global ViT tokens and high-resolution local patches, supporting semantic-edge-focused inference that reduces memory, latency and compute on very-high-resolution segmentation. SOTA accuracy is reported, but the abstract omits exact speedup/memory numbers, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: TriCCOT: Tri-part Convolutional Conformal Transformer for Onboard Space Object Detection
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / FPGA / efficient attention
p1_watchlist.why: TriCCOT replaces FPGA-unfriendly Transformer operations with convolutional projections, global channel statistics and hardware-friendly gating, and reports full unified CNN-Transformer deployment on a Xilinx Versal VCK190 without DPU modification. This is strong deployability evidence, but the primary abstract does not give measured latency, throughput, memory or energy gains, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: BIO-MEMART: Biometric-Aware KV Cache Memory for Multi-User LLM Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / efficient reasoning/agent systems / shared memory
p1_watchlist.why: Bio-MemArt adds biometric authorization to reusable KV-memory blocks while preserving MemArt latent retrieval and direct cache reuse. Its efficiency study reduces average prefill tokens from 18,781.96 full-context to 28.57, but the main novelty is access control rather than serving acceleration, so retain as a high-value KV/agent watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Safe Task Planning with Long-Term Graph Memory for Embodied Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / embodied agents / long-term memory / safety
p1_watchlist.why: CoRL 2026 SafeMem maintains a long-term semantic graph under partial observability and uses an LLM risk predictor plus conservatism-modulated replanning. It substantially improves safe success on IS-Bench and a real robot platform, making it a protected Physical-AI memory/safety node, but it reports no serving or compute-efficiency metric.

p1_watchlist.title: RoboCousin: Build Your Own Simulation Playground for Robust Bimanual Robotic Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / synthetic data systems / bimanual manipulation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI data-system work that converts user observations into simulation-ready assets, scenes, grasp-contact annotations and expert trajectories. RoboCousin-OBD contains over 3,000 object instances and 50 environments, and the pipeline generates over one million trajectories across 50 tasks with sim-to-real validation. It improves data scalability rather than inference latency, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: A Measurement Study of LLM Inference Trade-offs Across Edge Continuum Hardware
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / LLM inference / measurement
p1_watchlist.why: This controlled study measures accuracy, footprint, prefill latency, per-token latency and execution energy across Jetson AGX Orin and near-edge CPU/GPU nodes, including quantized open models and cloud GPT-4o as a reference. It provides useful placement and Pareto evidence but introduces no new serving mechanism, so retain as a high-value measurement watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Distribution-Consistent Inference for Dynamic Sparse Mixture-of-Experts
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / dynamic routing / sparse inference
p1_watchlist.why: Findings EMNLP 2026 identifies representation-scale shift when inference-time top-k is reduced and proposes lightweight layer-wise distribution alignment using calibration statistics. It recovers much of the lost quality while preserving dynamic sparse-routing efficiency with negligible overhead, but the primary abstract gives no concrete latency/FLOP/throughput reduction, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Scaling Post-Training Ternarisation to Qwen3-8B Capability Retention, Reproduction, Lossless Packing, and Packed Execution
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / ultra-low-bit LLM / packed execution / deployment characterization
p1_watchlist.why: Provides an end-to-end Qwen3-8B ternarisation and deployment characterization including lossless packing and direct packed execution at 15.52 tokens/s in 7.35 GiB. It is valuable negative/engineering evidence because the preliminary packed GEMV is still slower than FP16 cuBLAS, so it is retained as watch rather than promoted as an acceleration result.

p1_watchlist.title: Agentic ML Exploration (A-MLE) for Ads Ranking
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / ML infrastructure / autonomous experimentation / industrial ranking
p1_watchlist.why: Industrial autonomous ML-exploration system deployed across a portfolio of large-scale ads-ranking models, coordinating hypothesis generation, experiment execution, analysis and shared knowledge with sandboxed tools and human checkpoints. It directly targets the human-throughput bottleneck of ML iteration, but the primary abstract does not expose a clean quantitative latency, compute, or cost reduction, so it remains high-value watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: Drive by Hindsight and Foresight: Tool-Grounded Synergistic Reasoning over Hierarchical Memory for Autonomous Driving
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / autonomous driving / hierarchical memory / proactive tool invocation
p1_watchlist.why: Couples scene-level short-term memory, evolving long-term experience memory and adaptive tool invocation in a closed reasoning loop. Its 7B model reaches 79.09% MCQ on DriveLMM-o1, with short-term memory improving STSBench by 24.2 points and frozen-parameter long-term memory adding 3.57 MCQ points. It is valuable Physical-AI memory/tool-use evidence, but the reported contribution is capability rather than inference efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: Do Dynamic Routers Need Memory? HeRo: History-Aware Routing for Efficient LLM Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / dynamic layer routing / efficient LLM inference / router memory
p1_watchlist.why: 7d low-rank replay recovered a relevant dynamic-routing paper absent from authority. HeRo conditions token-wise FFN routing on an explicit history state built with linear attention; on Llama 3.1-8B it reports 100.24% dense-model aggregate performance while bypassing 26.87% of parameters, and 97.01% performance while bypassing 38.82%. Retained as high-value watch because the abstract does not report measured wall-clock latency or throughput gains.

p1_watchlist.title: WorldAgen: Unified State-Action Prediction with Test-Time World Model Training
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world models / test-time adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work unifying world-state prediction and action prediction with lightweight test-time training to adapt world dynamics in unseen environments. It improves CALVIN/LIBERO performance after a small number of test-time samples, but the primary abstract gives no measured test-time overhead, latency or throughput, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: OmniNav: Robust Long-Horizon Target Navigation in Dynamic Environments
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / long-horizon navigation / persistent scene memory / closed-loop recovery
p1_watchlist.why: Maintains an updatable 3D object scene memory, revises target beliefs under partial observability, and propagates execution feedback through hierarchical closed-loop recovery. It improves real-world pick-and-place success from 53.3% to 71.7% over an adapted open-loop baseline. This is strong protected evidence for persistent embodied memory and closed-loop execution, but it does not claim inference acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: KBBQ: A Predictive Noise Law and the Limits of Spectrum Flattening in FP4 Quantization
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / FP4 / W4A4 / transform-based quantization
p1_watchlist.why: High-value FP4 quantization work with a closed-form second-order noise law and Kappa-Braked Blockwise Quantization. Across four base models and two FP4 formats, KBBQ improves W4A4 quality over prior state of the art without additional deployment-time computation. The primary abstract does not report measured latency/throughput or memory speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Jacap: Robust KV Cache Eviction via Jacobian-Based Nonlinear Information Capacity Preservation
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / eviction / information geometry / cache compression
p1_watchlist.why: 7d low-rank replay recovered a theoretically grounded KV-cache eviction method absent from authority. Jacap derives a Jacobian information-capacity objective for nonlinear softmax attention and uses softmax-aware importance plus statistical leverage scores for cache subset selection, with strongest gains reported in high-compression regimes. Retained as high-value watch because the current evidence is quality-under-compression rather than measured serving latency/throughput.

p1_watchlist.title: Router Prior Bias: Preserving Base Routing Structure in MoE Post-Training
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / router post-training / expert co-activation
p1_watchlist.why: Shows downstream MoE post-training benefits from softly preserving the pretrained router prior rather than re-imposing uniform load balancing. Important expert-routing lineage on Moonlight-16B-A3B and Qwen3-30B-A3B, but no measured serving throughput/latency gain in the primary abstract.

p1_watchlist.title: Nyström Attention Matches Full Attention for Cross-Sectional Stock Prediction
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / low-rank attention / linear-complexity approximation
p1_watchlist.why: This controlled attention decomposition finds the learned cross-sectional attention deviation to be low-rank and shows Nystrom attention with 32 landmarks matches full O(N^2) attention at O(mN) cost, with statistical equivalence at N=300 and N=800. It is useful evidence for low-rank rather than sparse attention structure, but the primary abstract does not report measured latency, throughput, memory or energy gains, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Marigold V2: Revisiting Diffusion Transformers for Monocular Depth Estimation
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / dense vision / single-step inference
p1_watchlist.why: Marigold V2 converts pretrained multi-step flow-matching image models into single-step dense-regression inference, with quantization where needed, while improving KITTI/ETH3D AbsRel by 16-26% over the previous best. The step-count reduction is strategically relevant to diffusion/flow acceleration, but the current abstract does not report measured end-to-end latency or throughput, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: MetaKV: Adaptive KV Cache Compression for Constrained LLM Inference
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / adaptive compression / constrained inference
p1_watchlist.why: MetaKV predicts latency, peak memory, and correctness for multiple KV compression configurations and selects per-prompt settings under user budgets. Across KVQuant, H2O, RocketKV and FP16 it improves constrained success rate by about 0.07 on average and up to 0.135 over the best static configuration; useful systems direction, but the primary result is budget satisfaction rather than a direct end-to-end speedup, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Streaming Hierarchical Inference with Tabular Foundation Models
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / hierarchical inference / selective offloading
p1_watchlist.why: HINT combines sliding-window graph ANN retrieval at the edge with uncertainty-aware selective offloading to a cloud-hosted tabular foundation model, explicitly trading predictive quality against communication and latency. It is a clean edge-cloud inference pattern, but the current abstract reports favorable trade-offs without concrete throughput/latency gains, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: ReactVAU: A Slow-Fast Decoupled Framework for Streaming Video Anomaly Understanding
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming video / conditional MLLM invocation / persistent memory
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces a slow-fast streaming design where a lightweight detector continuously filters the stream, anomaly-aware persistent memory preserves rare events, and heavyweight MLLM reasoning wakes only on suspicious events. The paper explicitly reports substantially fewer heavyweight MLLM invocations and real-time streaming operation, but the primary abstract omits a single quantitative latency/throughput figure, so it is retained as a high-value serving watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: Interactive Debugger for Performance Portable Python HPC Kernels
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / Python HPC / developer tooling
p1_watchlist.why: PKDB adds breakpoints, stepping, inspection, live code evaluation and hot kernel substitution while preserving on-device PyKokkos execution across CPU/GPU backends. The primary abstract reports limited overhead but no quantified workload speedup; it is retained as high-value runtime/tooling infrastructure.

p1_watchlist.title: Quantization Amplifies Determinism, Not Bias: Scale-Dependent Behavioral Effects of Serving-Time Weight Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / LLM serving / behavioral fidelity
p1_watchlist.why: This controlled serving-time study compares Qwen3 8B/14B/32B under W4A16 AWQ, W8A16 FP8-Marlin and BF16 across about 71k paired completions, finding scale-dependent output concentration and stylistic drift. It is valuable deployment-quality evidence for quantization, but it does not claim a new quantization runtime or measured speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: The OCUDU dApp Platform: An Open Runtime and E3 Interface for Real-Time AI-RAN
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / real-time AI-RAN / GPU runtime / edge orchestration
p1_watchlist.why: Protected edge/heterogeneous replay recovered an open production-DU runtime that supports GPU-resident receive-chain apps, scheduler-path apps under a 100 us admitted deadline, and never-blocking observer apps. Live GB10 gNB validation shows all three classes running together without fallback. It is highly relevant real-time AI infrastructure, but the abstract does not provide a comparative throughput or speedup baseline, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Kalman Delta Networks: Uncertainty-aware Associative Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / long-context / constant-memory recurrent inference
p1_watchlist.why: KDN reformulates recurrent associative memory as a linear-Gaussian state-space model and introduces scan-compatible diagonal and isotropic approximations whose uncertainty recurrences admit associative scans with logarithmic parallel depth. It improves perplexity and downstream accuracy over strong linear-attention baselines, but the abstract does not report measured latency/throughput gains, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Real-Time dApps for AI-RAN: Measured Interface Requirements for Inline PHY and Slot-Level Control
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / AI-RAN / low-latency runtime interface
p1_watchlist.why: This work measures the interface requirements of AI-RAN dApps under live-cell load and shows that only in-process paths continue meeting 100-us control deadlines for bounded/inline workloads once the DU is active. It provides unusually concrete systems measurements and a released ABI, but is adjacent to the core ML-serving focus, so retain as high-value edge-infrastructure watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Accuracy is Not Enough: A Divergence-Based Approach to Evaluate Fidelity Loss in Quantized LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / deployment evaluation / distribution fidelity
p1_watchlist.why: A 120-run matrix across five foundation architectures and four reasoning benchmarks evaluates progressive quantization from BF16 to Q2_K using full-vocabulary JS/TV divergence rather than only argmax accuracy. It shows mixed-precision Q4_K generally preserves distribution fidelity better than Q4_0 at similar memory footprints. This is a useful deployment-quality diagnostic rather than a new acceleration method, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: ICI-VLA: In-Context Imitation with Spatiotemporally Aligned Demonstrations for Vision-Language-Action Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / test-time adaptation / retrieval-conditioned control
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work keeps the VLA fixed at inference and adapts through retrieved phase- and geometry-aligned micro-demonstrations, reaching 97.7% LIBERO, 60.4% RoboTwin 2.0 and 83.2% across four physical tasks. No measured serving latency/throughput benefit is reported, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Anti-Gravity Walking by a Flying Humanoid Robot via Thrust-Rate Input Whole-Body Model Predictive Control
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot control / real-time MPC / humanoid
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a real-time whole-body MPC implementation for a flying humanoid, including sparse optimal-control structure and hardware demonstration under contact switching. This is deployment-relevant compute/control evidence, but the abstract does not provide absolute controller latency, throughput, or a comparative runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: Functional-SLAM: Interaction-Aware Mapping with Online Functional Scene Graphs
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / online mapping / scene graphs
p1_watchlist.why: Functional-SLAM maintains functional scene graphs online rather than relying on offline reconstruction, with substantially improved runtime while retaining competitive accuracy and enabling topology-assisted loop closure. The lack of concrete latency/throughput values keeps it as a high-value Physical-AI watch.

p1_watchlist.title: MEMO: Multimodal Evidence Memory Organization for Long-Horizon LLM Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-horizon memory / multimodal evidence budgeting
p1_watchlist.why: Selects relevant evidence blocks and assigns them to textual, visual, or dual-channel carriers under a constrained working-memory budget. Across HotpotQA, 2WikiMultiHopQA, LoCoMo, and ALFWorld it reports fewer memory tokens with improved downstream performance, but the primary abstract gives no exact latency, token-reduction, or cost ratio, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: OpenWAM: An Open, Modular Exploration Towards Systematic World-Action Model Pretraining
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / WAM infrastructure / deployment stack
p1_watchlist.why: OpenWAM provides an open modular infrastructure that factorizes WAM model, representation, training, inference, deployment and evaluation choices, with released code, checkpoints, data recipes and real-robot evaluation across multiple embodiments. It is important infrastructure for the protected WAM direction, but the paper currently emphasizes modularity, scaling and task performance rather than measured serving speedup, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Fluent Generation: A CPU Reliability Benchmark for MCP-Style Tool Calling in Sub-2B Small Language Models for Edge Deployment
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / tool-using SLMs / CPU inference / reliability-resource tradeoff
p1_watchlist.why: Provides an explicit edge-agent resource baseline for sub-2B tool-calling models. Qwen2.5-1.5B uses 7,960 MiB and 30.782 s mean CPU latency versus 3,637 MiB and 10.627 s for Qwen2.5-0.5B, while reliability changes substantially. This is valuable deployment evidence but a benchmark rather than a new acceleration method, so it stays watch.

p1_watchlist.title: EnvPilot: Systematic Design and Evaluation of an Experience-Augmented Agent for Software Environment Setup
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / software engineering agents / trajectory memory / experience reuse
p1_watchlist.why: Maintains a trajectory-derived memory initialized with 667 validated experiences and retrieves prior setup strategies to avoid redundant exploration. On 112 real GitHub instances across nine languages it reaches 75% Pass@1 while the paper reports reduced reasoning cost, but the primary abstract does not expose a clean quantitative token/latency/cost reduction, so it remains a high-value watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: RouteRelay: Event-Triggered Cross-Layer Route Reuse for Efficient Dynamic Sparse Attention
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / sparse attention / route reuse / GPU kernels
p1_watchlist.why: RouteRelay reuses sparse-attention routing metadata across layers and selectively reroutes rows only when sentinel chunks challenge the retained route. It reaches at least 99.99% route recall and evaluates 38.4-51.6% of full-routing score pairs at larger routing scales, but its current unfused CPU implementation remains slower than dense matrix multiplication, so this is an important systems watch rather than canonical-high yet.

p1_watchlist.title: Separating Stream Stability from Long-Term Recall in Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / streaming LLM / constant-memory evaluation
p1_watchlist.why: ThreeH separates stability, access and utility horizons under a common state/compute budget and shows that attention-sink streaming can remain stable indefinitely while losing semantic access outside the active cache. It is an important systems-evaluation contract for constant-memory streaming and cache/recurrent/retrieval designs, but it does not introduce a new measured faster runtime, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: LightSplat: Real-Time High-Fidelity 3D Gaussian SLAM with Loop Closure
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / 3DGS / real-time SLAM
p1_watchlist.why: LightSplat combines sparse tracking with a dual-thread dense Gaussian backend and online loop closure, sustaining about 8 FPS on real-world robotic deployment while preserving reconstruction quality. It is directly relevant real-time 3DGS robotics infrastructure, but stronger comparative speedup evidence is still missing.

p1_watchlist.title: Dense Structural Compression of Transformers via Gauge-Correct Channel Removal
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / dense structural compression / efficient inference
p1_watchlist.why: GaugeLasso learns structurally removable transformer channels while retaining dense tensors suitable for GPU execution, achieving very large FMA compression on controlled tasks and discovering depth-dependent compact architectures. The evidence is scientifically interesting but currently centered on synthetic/statistical tasks without measured LLM-serving latency, so retain as watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Query-Aware Token Budgeting for Efficient Late-Interaction Visual Document Retrieval
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / retrieval systems / token compression
p1_watchlist.why: Uses a heavily compressed hot-path index followed by query-aware stage-two token budgeting over shortlisted pages, recovering 98.39% of full-token score with greedy marginal-gain selection under a pool-factor-eight-equivalent reranking budget. The latency analysis identifies practical operating points but the abstract gives no direct end-to-end speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: NutriBench-Kitchen: Benchmarking Embodied AI for Nutrition Management
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / persistent embodied memory / long-horizon kitchen agents
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces 1,500 manually verified QA pairs from 160 cooking videos covering ingredient entry, memory management, recipe query and long/short-term planning, explicitly testing whether embodied agents continuously maintain and use persistent food state. It fills a useful long-horizon memory benchmark gap but does not present serving or runtime-efficiency gains, so it is retained only as protected Physical-AI watch.

p1_watchlist.title: RoboDreamer: Anticipatory Humanoid Locomotion with Predictive State-Space Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / humanoid control / action chunking
p1_watchlist.why: RoboDreamer combines predictive state-space modeling, temporal masking/distillation and optional multi-step action chunking for robust humanoid locomotion, with real-time deployment on Unitree G1. The abstract indicates real-time latency but does not quantify serving speedup, so retain as a protected Physical-AI watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: NOVA-CIM: Noise- and Correlation-Tolerant Stochastic Interfaces for Analog Compute-in-Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / compute-in-memory / accelerator interfaces
p1_watchlist.why: Replaces multi-bit ADC readout with random-reference 1-bit sensing and lightweight stochastic counting for analog CIM, targeting energy-efficient inference while improving robustness to read noise and correlated stochastic inputs. End-to-end ViT-Base accuracy remains 84.48% versus 84.51% BF16 under modeled read noise, but no measured latency/energy speedup is reported, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: MEMOBench: A Process Level Memory Benchmark for Robotic Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot memory / benchmark
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI benchmark separates robot-memory Storage, Update and Compression across 30 history-dependent tasks, 1,500 demonstrations and 4,200 executable checkpoints; the strongest memory baseline reaches only 31.9% average success. It is important diagnostic infrastructure but not an efficiency-improving runtime, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: GIFT: Goal-Injected Fine-Tuning for Efficient Manipulation Policy Adaptation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / lightweight adaptation / goal-conditioned manipulation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work injects generated goal-image features into pretrained VLA policies through zero-initialized convolution; one epoch of fine-tuning improves reported task success by 4.7-13.4 percentage points. The efficiency claim is adaptation-oriented and the abstract lacks serving/runtime measurements, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Train Overcomplete, Deploy Compact: Scaling Recovery Capacity for Structured LLM Pruning
p1_watchlist.topic: sparsity/pruning / structured LLM pruning / recovery
p1_watchlist.why: OverRep temporarily overparameterizes the recovery module during training and algebraically merges it into an inference-time compact module. It improves retained reasoning by up to 5.5 and 8.4 points at 25% and 50% structured pruning while preserving the compact deployed architecture, but current evidence emphasizes quality recovery rather than measured latency, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Unified AI Gateway: A Framework for Joint Model Routing and KV Cache Management
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / model routing / KV cache management / edge-cloud placement
p1_watchlist.why: Unified AI Gateway jointly reasons about model choice, execution site, and KV-cache actions under quality, latency, cost and resource constraints, with analytical workload simulations reporting 1.25-13.28x TTFT and 1.20-6.16x input-cost benefits. It is strategically relevant but is primarily a synthesis/framework with simulation rather than a new measured deployed system, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Distributed Dexterous Manipulation with Spatially Conditioned Multi-Agent Transformers
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multi-agent transformer / dexterous manipulation
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work uses spatially conditioned Multi-Agent Transformers for an 8x8 array of 64 soft delta robots and introduces action selection that maintains real-world manipulation accuracy around 1.5 cm while using about 65% fewer robots. This is meaningful resource-use evidence, but the primary abstract does not report inference latency/throughput or compute speedup, so it remains watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: Characterizing Contention-Induced Reliability Collapse in KV-Cache Timing Side Channels for Multi-Tenant LLM Serving
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / LLM serving / multi-tenant security characterization
p1_watchlist.why: Seven experiments on live shared LLM serving show that KV-cache timing side-channel reliability collapses under realistic contention; on a two-node two-GPU tensor-parallel vLLM setup mean effect size drops from 3.418 to 0.511. This is valuable multi-tenant KV-cache systems characterization rather than an efficiency-improving runtime, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Diagnosing and Dynamically Filtering Occupancy World Models for Active Mapping
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world-model runtime / active mapping / occupancy filtering
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI/world-model work that isolates how occupancy completion errors alter both exploration choices and motion feasibility, then studies dynamic filtering of learned occupancy for active mapping. The planner is held fixed so the effect of the world-model representation is attributable, making this useful for world-model runtime reliability and selective-use policies. It does not present a direct serving or compute speedup metric in the primary abstract, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: BLINK: Batch Normalization-based Integrity Checkpoints for In-Situ Detection and Mitigation of Diverse Weight Corruptions in DNN Accelerators
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / accelerator reliability / runtime
p1_watchlist.why: BLINK performs autonomous on-chip inference-time corruption detection and mitigation without host intervention or fine-tuning data, with >99% detection precision and under 2% latency overhead. It is valuable accelerator-runtime resilience work but not primarily an efficiency contribution, so retain as watch.

p1_watchlist.title: ECOKV: Geometry-Aware KV Cache Eviction via Complementary Diversity Metrics
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache/long-context / multimodal MLLM serving / cache eviction
p1_watchlist.why: Directly relevant KV-cache compression work for multimodal LLMs: complementary Euclidean and cosine diversity metrics estimate per-head redundancy and adaptively balance diversity and importance while reducing the recent-token observation window. The primary abstract reports state-of-the-art quality across compression ratios but no measured end-to-end latency, throughput, or memory-speedup number, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: VLA-Corrector: Stage-Aware Observable State Understanding for Prompt-Based Closed-Loop Recovery of Vision-Language-Action Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / closed-loop recovery / runtime verifier
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work adds an observable-history Learned Verifier over multi-view vision, proprioception and executed actions, then produces stage-conditioned recovery prompts for the same frozen VLA policy without privileged simulator state. LIBERO and LIBERO Plus evaluations show substantially improved closed-loop reliability, but no measured serving overhead or throughput is reported in the primary abstract, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: DFlow: Enabling Verifier Information Flow in Block Diffusion Speculative Decoding
p1_watchlist.topic: speculative decoding / diffusion language models / verifier reuse
p1_watchlist.why: DFlow reuses verifier hidden states from rejected suffix positions across drafting rounds, so spent verifier computation informs later drafts without extra target computation, and self-conditioning teaches that cross-round information flow. It improves draft quality and acceptance length over DFlash on Qwen3, but the primary abstract gives no exact end-to-end throughput or latency speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: One MLLM, One Call: Efficient Zero-Shot Vision-and-Language Navigation via Spatial-Aware Waypoints
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / VLN / sparse MLLM invocation / robot navigation
p1_watchlist.why: O2C-Nav reduces zero-shot VLN-CE to a single MLLM call per decision step using structured waypoints, explicit spatial markers, and a low-level FMM planner, directly targeting inference latency and visual-processing overhead. It outperforms prior zero-shot methods and releases code, but the current primary abstract does not provide hard end-to-end latency/throughput numbers, so retain as protected high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Steering Under Compression: Dose-Response, Capability Cost, and Failure Asymmetry in Quantized LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / LLM deployment / activation steering / capability-cost characterization
p1_watchlist.why: Systematically studies inference-time activation steering under INT8 and NF4 across four open 7-9B models. It finds steering directions largely survive compression but capability-cost and failure behavior change substantially, including a Mistral-NF4 GSM8K baseline shift from 0.545 to 0.365. Valuable deployment characterization, but not a new acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: PACO: A Fully Cache-Oblivious Parallel FFT with One Global Redistribution
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training/inference / parallel FFT / communication-efficient HPC
p1_watchlist.why: PACO fuses deferred cache-oblivious layout changes into the single redistribution already required by the parallel FFT, proving optimal local cache complexity and exactly one global redistribution round under its ownership model. The current paper is primarily theoretical and exposes no measured end-to-end hardware speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: PLSR: Progressive and Localized Super-Resolution of 3D Objects via Localized Latent Voxel Diffusion
p1_watchlist.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / 3D generation / localized denoising / memory efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Decomposes global 3D super-resolution into localized latent-voxel diffusion subproblems with low-cost finetuning and patch-wise denoising, explicitly targeting memory and computational efficiency for high-resolution 3D generation. The primary abstract claims significant computational-cost reduction but gives no exact speedup or memory number, so it is kept as a high-value diffusion-efficiency watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: From Concentration to Differentiation and Back: Routing Effective Rank in MoE Reasoning Cohorts
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / efficient reasoning / routing characterization
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces routing effective rank as a label-free measure of cross-rollout MoE expert-routing organization during test-time scaling, with a reproducible low-high-low trajectory across ten MoE configurations and five reasoning benchmarks. This is useful systems characterization for dynamic routing and test-time compute policies, but it does not itself provide a serving speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Linear Algebra Foundations of Efficient Attention: A Phase Reversal in Rank Collapse Under SVD Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / low-rank compression / KV-cache lineage
p1_watchlist.why: Unifies low-rank attention/KV-cache compression literature and adds a controlled finding that SVD compression reverses its rank-collapse behavior between initialization and pretrained models. Useful compression-mechanism lineage, but it does not present a direct serving latency/throughput improvement, so it stays watchlist.

p1_watchlist.title: Query-Oblivious Coresets for Softmax Attention: Improved Bounds and Efficient Constructions
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient attention / attention coresets / theory
p1_watchlist.why: Constructs query-oblivious subsets of key-value pairs that approximate softmax attention uniformly over a query ball, improving coreset-size bounds and giving randomized polynomial-time constructions. This is directly relevant to principled attention compression, but current evidence is theoretical rather than measured accelerator/runtime speedup, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: SIDE: Sensor Impersonation Detection at the Edge via Sequence Prediction
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / edge inference / quantization / tiny ML
p1_watchlist.why: Deploys an LSTM detector on Arduino Nano 33 BLE and compares non-quantized, 16-bit, and 8-bit variants: model size falls from 554 KB to 298.5 KB and 185 KB, while the authors explicitly report quantization made execution slower in their measurements. This is a useful hardware-aware negative result for edge quantization, not a strong acceleration result.

p1_watchlist.title: MobileVLA-R1 2.0: RL-Enhanced Reasoning for Mobile Robot Control
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / mobile robot control / reasoning-action decoupling
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work coupling structured embodied reasoning with a reasoning-conditioned action decoder and embodiment-specific controllers, evaluated on navigation, quadruped control and real Unitree Go2/G1 deployments. It improves task success but reports no serving/runtime efficiency metric, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: RefGuard: Identity-Aware Language-Guided Robot Manipulation via Joint Target-Anchor-Frame Grounding
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / deployment reliability / grounding / robot runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Maintains a joint target-anchor-reference-frame posterior and defers execution when grounding is ambiguous. On a real UF850 arm it records zero identity switches on ambiguity-stress trials and 90.0% correct execution versus 33-46% identity-switch rates for baselines; protected deployment-reliability work rather than a compute acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: From Splats to Silicon: Rethinking Computational Efficiency of 3DGS
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / 3DGS acceleration / accelerator architecture
p1_watchlist.why: This workload-centric 3DGS systems study connects representation changes, GPU runtime optimization and hardware architecture, with reproduced measurements and controlled GPU profiling that trace workload counts into stage time and memory traffic. It is highly relevant to efficient-3DGS systems methodology, but its contribution is synthesis and characterization rather than a single new faster runtime, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Protocol Compression Changes Which Party Pays: Bilateral Cost in Cross-Organization LLM Agent Communication
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agent communication / protocol compression / token cost
p1_watchlist.why: Measures bilateral token and monetary cost of compressed protocols across six vendors and 1,053 completed cross-organization agent dialogues. Negotiated sessions cost 52% of the English baseline largely because they terminate sooner, while break-even horizons are 20-70 turns and some vendor pairs reverse which endpoint is cheaper. Valuable deployment economics and communication-efficiency evidence, but not a generally positive acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: Where Success Breaks: Failure-Boundary Learning for Robust Vision-Language-Action Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / robust adaptation / failure recovery
p1_watchlist.why: Frames robust VLA adaptation as discovering, localizing, and shaping failure boundaries rather than only fitting successful demonstrations. DLS uses real-grounded priors plus simulated co-training to expose recovery boundaries; retained as a protected deployment-robustness watch item because the main contribution is reliability rather than measured serving efficiency.

p1_watchlist.title: LayerRoute: Action-Conditioned Mixture-of-Layers Routing for Vision-Language-Action Policies
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / adaptive layer routing / cached VLM representations
p1_watchlist.why: LayerRoute dynamically mixes cached VLM-layer representations and rereads prior action states for VLA control, improving StarVLA-pi and pi0.5 across simulation and real-world benchmarks with only 0.31%/3.87% added parameters. It is highly relevant to adaptive representation access and cache reuse, but the current evidence emphasizes task quality rather than measured inference speedup, so retain as protected high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Retraining-Free MoE Compression: A Cost-Normalized Study of Post-Compression Adjustment
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / compression / deployment memory / adjustment cost
p1_watchlist.why: This study evaluates four MoE pruning/merging methods on two MoE LLM backbones with matched GPU-cost accounting and shows that a tiny one-epoch post-compression adjustment on 3,000 C4 examples recovers 37.3% of the original-to-compressed performance gap on average. It is useful deployment-efficiency evidence, but it does not provide a new serving runtime or measured latency/throughput speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: NSFlow: End-to-End Differentiable Neuro-Symbolic Optical Flow for Visual Odometry
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / embedded visual odometry / realtime perception / efficient robotics
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI replay recovered a hybrid CNN plus differentiable Lucas-Kanade optical-flow front-end that is explicitly designed for efficient VO/VIO and reports realtime embedded deployment with lower latency than purely regression-based alternatives. The abstract does not expose a directly comparable absolute latency or speedup figure, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: FALCON-S: Fixed-wing ground-effect Aerodynamics Simulator and Flight Control Learning Suite
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / GPU simulation / robot learning
p1_watchlist.why: FALCON-S provides modular high-fidelity 6DoF fixed-wing ground-effect simulation with CPU and NVIDIA Warp GPU backends and high-throughput parallel execution for RL and optimal-control rollouts. It is valuable Physical-AI simulation infrastructure, but the abstract gives no comparative throughput figures.

p1_watchlist.title: LoGIC: Budgeted Context Construction for Node-Level Graph In-Context Learning with Tabular Foundation Models
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / efficient attention / context budgeting / graph in-context learning
p1_watchlist.why: LoGIC targets the quadratic attention, preprocessing, and memory bottlenecks caused by using the full labeled training table as graph-ICL context. It allocates labeled-context and unlabeled-halo budgets, shares context within graph-local query clusters, and reports markedly lower peak memory while preserving locally runnable full-context performance and enabling frozen graph ICL on million-node graphs. The primary abstract lacks an exact latency or memory-reduction factor, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Rethinking the Evaluation of Efficiency Methods for Multi-Agent Systems
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent efficiency / evaluation methodology
p1_watchlist.why: Directly audits claimed efficiency gains in LLM multi-agent systems under a shared backbone, agent registry, runtime, topology, scale, depth, and tool-use controls. It shows that apparent gains can come from structural collapse, disabled tool pathways, or weak starting systems where random pruning already preserves accuracy. This is important for evaluating agent-efficiency papers, but it is primarily a diagnostic benchmark rather than a new acceleration method, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: CR-VLA-Force: Learning Control-aware Compliance VLA Model for Robust Contact-rich Robotic Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal MoE / reactive control
p1_watchlist.why: CR-VLA-Force explicitly targets the latency and action-chunk limitations of force-aware VLA control using a multimodal MoE plus VLA-guided adaptive compliance controller, and validates on real contact-rich tasks. It is accepted by IEEE RA-L and highly relevant to reactive Physical-AI deployment, but the current primary abstract does not provide measured end-to-end latency or throughput numbers, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Distilling Vision-Language Models for On-Device Fire Understanding
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / edge inference / VLM distillation
p1_watchlist.why: This work distills domain-specialized VLMs into compact students and deploys them on a commercial Detectium fire sensor, jointly measuring reasoning accuracy, latency and memory. It is valuable real-device MLLM deployment evidence, but the abstract does not report a concrete speedup or latency reduction, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Inference-Time Graph Engineering for Multi-Agent LLM Workflows
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent orchestration / inference-time workflow graphs
p1_watchlist.why: ReActNet compiles each query into task-conditioned temporal communication graphs with edge-level message semantics, separating graph compilation from execution without RL or gradient-based topology optimization. It improves multiple reasoning and assistant tasks while maintaining competitive inference cost, but the abstract gives no exact cost or latency reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: RAGMark: A Comprehensive Framework for Benchmarking Retrieval-Augmented Generation Systems
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / RAG systems / benchmarking
p1_watchlist.why: RAGMark is a modular multi-GPU RAG benchmark collecting per-stage latency, TTFT, throughput, GPU utilization, memory, power and quality. Its experiments expose cross-stage bottleneck shifts and show reranking plus compression can lower energy by up to 66%, but the contribution is primarily measurement infrastructure rather than a new serving mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: Beyond Scalar Flexibility: From Eligible AI Workloads to Dependable Load Relief
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / datacenter power / workload flexibility
p1_watchlist.why: Reconstructs 4,439 hourly power observations from a 185-day trace of 155,410 GPUs and derives duration/reliability-aware AI workload flexibility. Valuable production-scale AI-infrastructure power characterization, but not an ML acceleration technique.

p1_watchlist.title: Towards Neuro-Symbolic Procedural Reasoning for Long-Horizon Vision-Language-Action Manipulation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / long-horizon VLA / procedural memory
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work combining learned VLA control with explicit task graphs and multimodal procedural memory to maintain long-horizon task state, dependencies, conditional branches and visual evidence. It is an ECCV 2026 workshop extended abstract and does not report compute-side speedup, so it is retained as a high-value watch for VLA runtime/state architecture rather than promoted strong.

p1_watchlist.title: RoboSPA: Can VLA Models Go Beyond Simple Scenes and Short-Horizon Tasks?
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / benchmark / long-horizon embodied reasoning
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI benchmark with 10 task categories, 56 base tasks, 280 difficulty variants and 527K trajectories across multiple embodiments. It exposes spatial, execution, and memory-intensive planning failures in current VLAs and provides official data/code, but it is primarily a diagnostic benchmark rather than an efficiency/runtime contribution, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Temporal Tactile Encoding and Compliance for Intent-Aware Robot-to-Human Bimanual Handover
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / multimodal VLA / tactile control
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work coupling a VLA model with temporal tactile encoding, proprioception, and a compliance controller for intent-aware bimanual handover. Human-subject evaluation shows complementary gains over visual-only and tactile-without-compliance baselines, but no measured inference latency or compute reduction is reported, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Testing Interchangeability in LLM Agent Teams
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / multi-agent communication / coordination cost
p1_watchlist.why: Shows that swapping role-matched agents can preserve task score while increasing communication per unit progress by 16-63%, with larger penalties after longer team formation. This is useful systems characterization of hidden multi-agent coordination cost, but not an acceleration method.

p1_watchlist.title: One Word, Different Action: A Real-Robot Benchmark for Language-Conditioned Embodied Reasoning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / real-robot benchmark / language-conditioned action reasoning
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces a real-robot benchmark that separates decision invariance from decision sensitivity under minimal instruction changes, multi-constraint reasoning, and real-RGB grounding. It exposes failures when multiple constraints must be composed into one executable action, making it useful protected Physical-AI coverage, but it is a benchmark rather than an inference-efficiency method.

p1_watchlist.title: Compact Neural Appearance Models for Efficient Gaussian Splatting
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / 3DGS / compact appearance representation / CUDA rendering
p1_watchlist.why: Performs an end-to-end comparison of spherical-harmonic and learned spherical appearance models inside one optimized differentiable CUDA rasterizer, and introduces compact per-primitive latent codes decoded by a tiny shared MLP. The representation directly targets per-primitive storage and memory traffic and includes rendering-performance evaluation, but the primary abstract does not expose a single quantitative speedup or memory-reduction figure, so it remains a protected high-value watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: Proton Irradiation Characterization of an Open-Source ML Accelerator on a Zynq UltraScale+ MPSoC
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / Physical AI / FPGA accelerator reliability
p1_watchlist.why: System-level proton-irradiation study of an open-source Tensil neural-network accelerator on Zynq UltraScale+ running ResNet-20 inference, documenting availability loss and silent output corruption with implications for recovery and verifiable edge/space AI deployment. Important Physical-AI/edge accelerator reliability evidence, but not primarily an efficiency or acceleration contribution.

p1_watchlist.title: ACE: Adaptive Calibration-Free Expert Skipping for MoE-based LLMs
p1_watchlist.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / adaptive expert skipping
p1_watchlist.why: Training- and calibration-free token-adaptive expert skipping with offline spectral/prototype statistics and lightweight runtime table lookups. Strong quality at 50% expert skipping across multiple MoE LLMs, but current abstract lacks measured end-to-end systems speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: LIBERO-RECOVER: Beyond Task Success Towards Failure Recovery in Robotic Manipulation Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / evaluation / failure recovery / robustness
p1_watchlist.why: Introduces 1,000+ real execution-failure scenarios on LIBERO across action retry, adaptation, object-state recovery, and environmental recovery, explicitly targeting VLA/WAM deployment robustness beyond nominal task success. It is a protected Physical-AI benchmark rather than a compute/serving acceleration paper, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: APEX-RBD: Mixed-Precision Exploration Framework for Hardware-Efficient Robot Dynamics Accelerator Design
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robot accelerator / mixed precision / edge hardware
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI hardware-efficiency candidate. Automates mixed-precision design-space exploration for rigid-body-dynamics accelerators and reports up to 1.9x area reduction and 1.8x power savings across robotic platforms; valuable but focused on dynamics hardware rather than learned policy serving.

p1_watchlist.title: Compression Beyond the Uncompressed: A Two-Stage Training Recipe for Soft Context Compression in RAG
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / RAG / soft context compression / inference efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: DEX-Comp directly targets the inference overhead of long retrieved contexts by encoding documents into substantially shorter embedding sequences. Its two-stage recipe first distills correct uncompressed-RAG behavior, then uses RL only on cases the uncompressed system fails. This is highly relevant to serving efficiency, but the primary abstract emphasizes QA quality across retrieval depths and does not provide a measured latency/throughput or token-cost reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: MomentQuant: an even more minimalist interval method with linear time complexity for time series classification
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / efficient inference / linear-time algorithms
p1_watchlist.why: MomentQuant replaces exact interval quantiles with Cornish-Fisher approximations, removes the sorting requirement and reduces inference complexity to linear time. The primary abstract reports the optimized Quant implementation is faster than the original and MomentQuant is faster again with only a tiny predictive-performance decrease, making it relevant to lightweight inference; however, no numeric deployment latency/throughput gain is given in the primary abstract, so it remains watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: A Schema Bounded Language Model for Refining Robot Policies Without Destabilizing Local Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / hierarchical agent runtime / decentralized robot control
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime work that cleanly separates expensive LLM reasoning from fast local control: LLM inference is confined to round-level policy generation/refinement while a UCB bandit and policy-conditioned Double DQN execute tick-level actions. In the evaluated three-robot simulation, the complete configuration reached all 90 robot-round goals and achieved 42-tick median completion time, 25.0-39.1% lower than alternative configurations. The evidence is simulation-level task efficiency rather than measured inference latency/throughput, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Compact Bellman-Grounded Cognitive Maps for Cost-Aware Navigation
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / navigation memory / compact world representation / cost-aware planning
p1_watchlist.why: Learns a reusable Bellman-grounded cognitive map with compact coordinate encoding, enabling changing navigation goals without per-goal retraining. On grids up to 1,600 nodes it maintains full success with only 5% mean gap to Dijkstra, while memory growth is sublinear from 400 to 3,600 nodes. It is valuable protected evidence for compact embodied memory, but not a direct VLA/WAM inference accelerator.

p1_watchlist.title: Deep Microcompression: Structured Pruning and Bit-packed Quantization for Microcontrollers
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / microcontroller inference / pruning / quantization
p1_watchlist.why: Hardware-aware MCU deployment pipeline combining structured pruning, QAT and fixed-length bit-packing; reports 55.8x weight compression and deployment on ATmega328P with 2KB SRAM. Valuable edge-AI systems signal but currently limited-model/MCU scope.

p1_watchlist.title: Efficient Multi-Timescale Event Representations for Feed-Forward Object Detection
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / event perception / feed-forward detection / neuromorphic efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: Encodes multi-timescale temporal information directly in event representations and introduces a recursive approximation for efficient event-by-event updates, reducing reliance on recurrent temporal modeling while preserving detection performance. The primary abstract does not quantify latency, throughput, or energy gains, so it remains a protected Physical-AI watch item.

p1_watchlist.title: EnvCraft: Synthesizing Executable Environments in Agentic RL for Claw-like Agent
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / agentic RL / executable environments / training infrastructure
p1_watchlist.why: Automates sandboxed executable-environment synthesis and topology-aware task generation, producing 139 environments and about 20K complex tasks. Qwen3/3.5 8B-32B models gain up to 11.9% on Claw benchmarks and 8.0% on tool-use benchmarks with reduced inference token cost, but the abstract does not quantify the cost reduction.

p1_watchlist.title: GreenPipe: Power Modeling for Containerized DNN Inference on Kubernetes Edge Nodes
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud heterogeneous AI systems / Kubernetes inference / online power modeling / energy-aware serving
p1_watchlist.why: 30d edge/heterogeneous replay recovered a current containerized inference systems paper absent from authority/watch. GreenPipe builds an automated external-meter profiling, regression-model training and validation pipeline for Raspberry-Pi/K3s DNN serving, covering precision/thread/local-vs-remote configurations and jointly reporting latency and energy. Retained as high-value watch because it is primarily measurement/modeling infrastructure rather than a new serving scheduler or accelerator mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: MCPO: Modality-Contrastive Preference Optimization for Multimodal Chain-of-Thought Compression
