p1_watchlist.why: Lightweight 0.6B zero-shot inference router preserves decoder KV across sessions and evaluates transient candidate labels without polluting persistent cache; directly relevant to serving model selection, but current primary evidence emphasizes routing quality rather than end-to-end latency/cost measurements.

p1_watchlist.title: SCULPT: Training Edge Vision Models for Post-Training Quantization Readiness
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / edge AI / deployment
p1_watchlist.why: SCULPT shapes activation distributions during ordinary FP32 training so models are easier to post-train quantize, exporting learned clipping bounds to standard INT8/W4A8 deployment without runtime transforms. It reports a large W8A8 accuracy recovery on EfficientNet-B0, but has limited systems-scale latency evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: Scaling Bimanual Household Manipulation from 1,500 hours of Demonstrations to On-Policy Corrections
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / bimanual manipulation / data pipeline / training efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: 7d protected Physical-AI replay recovered XR-2 and its 1,500-hour bimanual demonstration corpus. The work explicitly uses a purpose-built high-throughput data pipeline and multi-stage training paradigm and reports favorable training efficiency/data utilization, but the current abstract lacks comparative throughput/latency or systems-speedup numbers, so it is retained as high-value watch rather than promoted strong.

p1_watchlist.title: Scalable Kronecker-Fisher Approximation: Efficient Hessian Analysis for Billion-Parameter Language Models Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / sparsity / compression / Hessian-Fisher analysis
p1_watchlist.why: Scalable Kronecker-based Fisher/Hessian approximation captures cross-layer sensitivity for billion-parameter models without materializing the full matrix and correlates with degradation/recovery under quantization and sparsification. Useful for mixed-precision and sparsity allocation, but current contribution is analysis/methodology rather than demonstrated end-to-end serving acceleration.

p1_watchlist.title: S2-MoE: Enabling Efficient Self-Speculative Decoding for Mixture-of-Experts on Edge Devices
RVSD: Retrieval Vision Sparse Decoding for Mitigating Visual Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / sparse decoding / visual token retrieval
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free single-pass LVLM decoding combines semantics-directed visual-token sparsification with on-demand semantic-space visual retrieval, explicitly avoiding multi-round decoding overhead while retaining long-context hallucination suppression. Relevant inference design, but current public evidence is quality-centric and lacks hard end-to-end latency/throughput gains.

p1_watchlist.title: RoofGS: Roofline-Guided End-to-End Acceleration of 3D Gaussian Splatting
p1_watchlist.topic: 3D Gaussian Splatting / roofline / GPU kernels
p1_watchlist.why: Roofline-guided memory- and instruction-bottleneck co-optimization reaches 10.1x end-to-end speedup at 4K with negligible PSNR loss; valuable adjacent graphics/AI-inference systems work.

p1_watchlist.title: RoboTok: An Internet-Scale Data Engine for Human Demonstration Retrieval and Dexterous Manipulation Learning
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / data engine / scalable demonstration retrieval
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work builds an internet-scale motion-retrieval data engine using compact actor-centered 3D hand-trajectory embeddings for efficient search and continual indexing, and improves downstream dexterous manipulation policy success. The available primary description does not quantify retrieval latency/throughput or systems speedup, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Risk-Adaptive Edge--Cloud Visual Reasoning for Communication-Efficient Autonomous Driving
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / edge-cloud inference / autonomous driving / selective VLM offload
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI edge/cloud systems watch. An onboard VLM plus lightweight detector decide when cloud VLM reasoning is needed while safety-critical validation/control remain local. CARLA experiments match periodic-cloud task success while cutting cloud requests by 54.1% and evaluate multiple network profiles. Strong edge-cloud execution relevance, but the runtime mechanism is comparatively simple, so retain as high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: ReWorld: An Interactive World Model with Long-Horizon Memory
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / interactive world model / bounded KV cache / real-time streaming
p1_watchlist.why: Direct Physical-AI/world-model systems relevance: fixed-budget KV cache plus pose-indexed landmark retrieval enables minute-long interactive rollouts while maintaining real-time streaming and bounded memory.

p1_watchlist.title: Rethinking Language's Role in Efficient VLA for Autonomous Vehicles: Toward Smarter, Trustworthy Driving
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / autonomous driving / inference efficiency survey
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI survey/taxonomy centered on where language should remain at inference time under onboard latency, memory, FLOPs and token budgets. Useful landscape and lineage source, but it is primarily a survey rather than a new serving/runtime mechanism, so retain as high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: RealisticTritonBench: A Benchmark for Triton-Kernel Generation in Real-World AI Frameworks
p1_watchlist.topic: GPU kernel / Triton / compiler-agent benchmark / systems evaluation
p1_watchlist.why: High-value GPU-kernel/DSL watch item. RealisticTritonBench derives Triton generation tasks from real pull requests in production AI frameworks and evaluates generated kernels after integration with end-to-end framework tests, addressing isolated-kernel and weak-correctness limitations of prior benchmarks. Strong lineage/benchmark value, but primarily an evaluation benchmark rather than a new serving/runtime optimization mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: Real-Time Shape Control of Multi-Segment Soft Robotic Arms Using Koopman Operators with Global and Local Observables
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / real-time robot control / model-based runtime
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime work: a Koopman-MPC controller combines global and local observables for real-time full-shape control, scales numerically to 10 independently actuated segments, and is physically validated on 3- and 5-segment arms at tip speeds up to 0.6 m/s, with robustness to 400 g payloads and 7 N disturbances. It is a strong real-time control result, but not a serving/computation speedup paper, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Read Less, Solve More: Token-Efficient Sparse Reading for AI Agents
p1_watchlist.topic: efficient reasoning / agent systems / context admission / latency
p1_watchlist.why: Training-free pre-context sparse-reading layer for agents; reports up to 92.9% token reduction and 89.0% wall-time reduction across frontier models while preserving or improving task quality.

p1_watchlist.title: RACE-AIMC: Selective Inference for Heterogeneous Analog In-Memory Accelerators at the Edge
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / analog in-memory accelerator / selective inference
p1_watchlist.why: Relevant heterogeneous edge-AI accelerator routing framework with certified selective inference and modeled 69.02% energy reduction versus always running all accelerators, but current evidence is simulation-only and lacks a strong systems venue, so retain as high-value watch rather than canonical-high.

p1_watchlist.title: R2S-Eval: Robot Evaluation with Real-to-Sim Calibration via Vision-Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / evaluation infrastructure / real-to-sim
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI evaluation infrastructure calibrates simulation to a real setup and uses VLM preference judgments to reduce repeated hardware trials and operator effort while producing stable policy rankings. Real and simulated experiments support the workflow, but the abstract gives no exact evaluation-time or hardware-effort reduction, so it remains watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Quality Recovery for Quantized KV Caches via Low-Rank Attention Adaptation
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache / quantization / long-context inference / low-rank adaptation
p1_watchlist.why: High-value KV-quantization watch item. It keeps physically packed low-bit cache formats fixed and distills floating-cache behavior into low-rank Q/K/V projection updates, recovering substantial held-out perplexity gaps across multiple models/quantizers while showing that perplexity recovery does not necessarily recover long-context retrieval. Useful evidence for quantized-KV deployment tradeoffs, but currently narrower and more adaptation-centric than a new serving runtime mechanism.

p1_watchlist.title: PuzzleKV: Page-Wise Low-Rank Decomposition for KV Cache Compression
p1_watchlist.topic: KV cache / low-rank compression / autoregressive decode
p1_watchlist.why: Training- and calibration-free page-wise low-rank KV compression with direct attention over dense and factorized pages; retains >96% Full-KV performance around 60% storage and can combine with quantization for 18.7% storage.

p1_watchlist.title: ProxyFormer: A Dual-Stream Proxy Architecture for Ultra-Long Context and High-Resolution Generation
p1_watchlist.topic: long context / KV-cache reduction / high-resolution generation
p1_watchlist.why: Direct long-context efficiency work: proxy-only global interaction and proxy-only KV-cache inference extend trainable context from ~20K to ~0.7M on a 16GB GPU and support million-token retrieval.

p1_watchlist.title: Prism-GRPO: Faster VLA Policy Optimization via Splitting Same-outcome Groups
p1_watchlist.topic: Physical AI / VLA RL rollout efficiency
p1_watchlist.why: VLA GRPO rollout-efficiency method; reaches target success with up to 56% fewer rollouts, but contribution is primarily RL algorithm rather than serving/runtime.

p1_watchlist.title: PRIMAL: Processing-In-Memory Based Low-Rank Adaptation for LLM Inference Accelerator
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM inference accelerator / processing-in-memory / LoRA / edge AI
p1_watchlist.why: Direct PIM-based LLM inference accelerator integrating LoRA with heterogeneous PIM PEs, reprogramming/power-gating and dataflow orchestration. Retained as high-value watch pending stronger venue/independent adoption evidence.

p1_watchlist.title: Predictive Zonotope Reduction: Precise Runtime Monitoring under Uncertainty
p1_watchlist.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / runtime monitoring / edge safety
p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI runtime work dynamically selects zonotope reduction via beam-search MPC and distills the policy into a small neural policy for substantially faster execution while maintaining improved monitoring precision. Implemented in RLola and evaluated on Raspberry Pi 5 for a robotic-arm workload. The primary abstract lacks an exact latency/speedup number, so it remains high-value watch rather than strong.

p1_watchlist.title: Precision-Induced Miscalibration: Understanding and Correcting Confidence Distortion in Quantized Neural Networks
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / low-precision calibration / confidence distortion / mixed precision
p1_watchlist.why: ICML 2026 quantization-adjacent work. It characterizes confidence/gradient distortion caused by low precision and proposes PACS with sub-1% overhead. Relevant to deployment robustness, but the main contribution is calibration rather than model/runtime efficiency, so retain as high-value watchlist rather than canonical Efficient-ML systems lineage.

p1_watchlist.title: PPO-STGNN: A Proximal Policy Optimization Approach with Spatio-Temporal Graph Neural Networks for DAG Task Scheduling in Cloud-Edge-End Computing
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / scheduling / reinforcement learning
p1_watchlist.why: DAG scheduling across heterogeneous cloud-edge-end resources using STGNN state encoding plus PPO and multi-teacher behavior-cloning pretraining. Experiments report better load balancing while maintaining low completion time, but the primary abstract provides no exact latency/makespan gain, so this remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Post-Training Ternarization of Qwen3-4B Capability, Effective Bit Budget, Storage Compression, and Deployment
p1_watchlist.topic: quantization / LLM deployment / edge systems
p1_watchlist.why: This study converts Qwen3-4B to 1.641 effective bits per quantized linear weight and packs the model from 8.29 GiB to 3.96 GiB, explicitly auditing deployment behavior. It is valuable as a negative systems result because its preliminary Triton GEMV is 4.6x slower than FP16 cuBLAS, showing storage compression does not automatically yield inference speedup.

p1_watchlist.title: Pipeline-Native Transformers: Co-Designing Model Architecture and CPU Inference for Bandwidth-Efficient Autoregressive Decode
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / CPU inference / architecture-runtime co-design / MoE
p1_watchlist.why: CPU-first model/runtime co-design for memory-bandwidth-bound decode; reports 2x critical-path weight-bandwidth reduction and 5.94 tok/s on a 30.9B pipeline-native MoE, ahead of compared CPU backends.

p1_watchlist.title: Performance Foundations of Parallel & Distributed Reasoning Language Models
p1_watchlist.topic: distributed training / efficient reasoning / RL-for-LLM systems / parallelism
p1_watchlist.why: Compute-centric systems analysis of RL-for-LLM post-training. It formalizes work/depth/memory costs and systematizes intra-/inter-model parallelism, disaggregated placement, stage fusion, hybrid parallelism, and asynchronous execution. Directly relevant to efficient reasoning and distributed AI infrastructure, but primarily a systems taxonomy/guideline paper rather than a new runtime implementation, so retained as high-value watchlist rather than PROMOTE_STRONG.

The sparse adaptive 3D memory is structurally relevant to efficient world-model generation, but the primary abstract does not report a concrete latency, throughput, or memory reduction, so it remains high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Network-Aware Forecasting on Wireless Access Points
p1_watchlist.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / on-device inference / resource contention
p1_watchlist.why: Useful real deployment measurement for inference sharing an enterprise AP with packet processing. Five implementations run 6.1-19.1x slower on target AP than Raspberry Pi 5; two similarly sized foundation models differ 19x in AP latency; 13-stream serving under network saturation raises p99 RTT 76% and cuts throughput 7.06%. Primarily a measurement/deployability study rather than a new runtime, so watchlist-high.

p1_watchlist.title: More GPUs or a Smaller Cache? Tensor Parallelism versus KV Compression for Memory-Bound LLM Serving
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / KV cache / tensor parallelism / cost-performance
p1_watchlist.why: Direct serving trade-off study placing tensor parallelism and KV compression on one cost-normalized axis across A100/A40/H100; reports compression 1.20-2.00x cheaper below the weight-residency wall while TP is required above it.

p1_watchlist.title: MoE-ViE: Mixture of Experts Vision Encoder for Efficient Image and Video Understanding

p1_watchlist.why: Meta MoE vision encoder combines fine-grained expert scaling with a specialized inference kernel; largest model matches a 1.7x larger encoder at 76% latency and ships official code.

p1_watchlist.title: Modeling What Changes: Sparse, Residual World Models for Object-Centric Manipulation

p1_watchlist.why: Sparse change-gated residual world model predicts only changing objects, giving 8.6-11.1x fewer parameters and 2.5-4.6x better next-state pose accuracy than a dense baseline on 3-8 object MuJoCo pushing, with lower rollout drift and cross-object-count transfer. Strong Physical-AI efficiency signal, but planning success remains early and no deployment/runtime latency is shown, so retain as protected high-value watch.

p1_watchlist.title: Minima-KV: Retention-Preserving KV Cache Compression with Mixed-Format Paged Attention

p1_watchlist.title: Memory-Sovereign Inference: Output-Exact Execution Beyond Full Residency
p1_watchlist.topic: LLM serving / storage-backed inference / memory hierarchy / exactness
p1_watchlist.why: Storage-backed inference study with explicit resource/exactness accounting; demonstrates output-exact asynchronous execution beyond full residency and large wall-time reduction versus a blocking direct path in the named configuration.

p1_watchlist.why: Reusable 3D memory-tree avoids reprocessing entire video stream per query; direct embodied inference-efficiency relevance, but runtime/latency evidence needs deeper review.

Retained as high-value watch rather than canonical-high because its main contribution is benchmarking/evaluation infrastructure rather than a new compression or serving algorithm.

Current paper emphasizes policy/task quality more than measured end-to-end serving latency, so keep as high-value watch.

Scales to a 30B VLM while substantially reducing total and activated memory parameters, but current evidence emphasizes model/parameter efficiency rather than measured serving latency or throughput.

p1_watchlist.why: Protected Physical-AI work that explicitly models VLA inference delay. ARLI restores near-Markovian structure under asynchronous action generation and enables effective RL finetuning when standard RL fails under latency.

tracking_records.title: HybridFLow: SDN-Orchestrated Client Partitioning for Hybrid Federated Learning
tracking_records.topic: distributed training / edge-cloud / federated learning / network-aware scheduling
tracking_records.why: Closed-loop SDN orchestration estimates per-client communication time and partitions synchronous versus asynchronous FL clients using network-wide bottleneck visibility. Across multiple topologies it reaches 80% target accuracy 33-40% faster than SmartFLow and cuts average round duration by 30-40 seconds.

tracking_records.title: PACE: Perceived-Latency-Aware Cascading Service Routing and Filler Control for QoE-Efficient Retrieval-Augmented Dialogue Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / RAG serving / Physical AI cloud-edge runtime / dialogue systems
tracking_records.why: PACE jointly controls response-source routing, filler content and volatility-aware cache admission and is deployed on a humanoid-robot sales service. On 75k CarQA requests it halves pure-LLM P95 perceived time-to-first-response (0.29 vs 0.53s at c16), reaches 0.41s P95 and 2.4x lower latency than RAG at high load with equal quality, cuts filler calls by 94%, and eliminates stale answers in the reported setup.

tracking_records.title: Stencil Computation at the Intersection of AI and HPC
tracking_records.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / tensor compiler / heterogeneous GPU / HPC-AI convergence
tracking_records.why: Applies AI tensor-compiler abstractions from TinyTC and Triton to an 8th-order 25-point stencil across Intel, NVIDIA and AMD GPUs. On Intel B580, TinyTC reaches 15.6 Gpts/s versus 13.5 Gpts/s for PyTorch/Triton under random initialization, with zero-initialized runs reaching 35.8 Gpts/s through hardware memory compression; the study also exposes bandwidth and cache-management effects. This is direct measured compiler/runtime throughput evidence.

tracking_records.title: Decoupled Self-Forcing Distillation for Streaming Talking Head Generation
tracking_records.topic: video/image generation acceleration / streaming diffusion / causal distillation
tracking_records.why: Decouples low-dimensional causal motion generation from a distilled causal diffusion renderer and runs both as parallel streams. Reports 15.4 FPS at 1.3 s latency with no quality degradation, directly addressing streaming generative inference efficiency.

tracking_records.title: Maverick: Private and Verifiable LLM Inference Made Practical via Matrix-Vector Multiplication Delegation
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / private inference / verifiable delegation / heterogeneous offload
tracking_records.why: End-to-end Qwen3-4B prototype delegates dominant matrix-vector products while preserving input privacy and verifiability with virtually no server verification overhead. With one client thread, throughput improves up to 17x with online privacy masks, 45x with precomputed masks, and 44x for verification-only; client-side microbenchmarks with simulated network delay reach 12-157x depending on mode.

tracking_records.title: LiteRAG: Cost-Efficient Graph-Based Retrieval-Augmented Generation
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / RAG / retrieval efficiency / context reduction
tracking_records.why: Replaces retrieval-time LLM control with query-conditioned graph exploration and reasoning-chain context construction. On DistComp it cuts per-query latency by over 100x and cost by over 99% versus GraphRAG Global and DRIFT while achieving the best reported overall quality; on UltraDomain it matches LinearRAG quality with about 14x fewer tokens. This is direct measured RAG serving efficiency evidence.

tracking_records.title: Kernel-Managed Shared Memory for System-Wide Personalization
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory / agent runtime / context management
tracking_records.why: AIOS kernel-managed shared memory centralizes retrieval, privacy enforcement, and prompt injection across agents. Across GPT-4o, Llama-3.1-8B, and Qwen2.5-7B in 1,800 trials, it approaches full-context personalization while using much shorter prompts and reduces end-to-end latency by 15-61%, with corresponding token and inference-cost reductions.

tracking_records.title: SAGE: Semantic-Aware Geographic Error Recovery for AI Data Movement
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / AI interconnect / fault recovery / communication latency
tracking_records.why: Semantic-aware replay architecture distinguishes catastrophic from quantization-like numerical faults and adapts replay restart geography. gem5 Garnet plus ASAP7 evaluation reports 30.1% lower quality-normalized terminal latency than fixed 34-hop recovery, including 28.0% lower mean latency, bounded queues under higher-BER stress, and lower DeiT-S mean/p99.5 latency.

tracking_records.title: GraphDroid: Asynchronous LLM-Based Mobile App GUI Testing via History-Aware Exploration and Hybrid Intent Fulfillment
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / asynchronous LLM agents / GUI testing / cost-aware tool use
tracking_records.why: Uses history-aware cluster memory, asynchronous intent generation, and hybrid fulfillment that reserves the LLM for complex intents while routing simple intents to a lightweight heuristic. Across 41 Android apps it achieves up to 36.4% higher code coverage while costing less than one eighth of the best pure-LLM baseline, directly addressing LLM-agent latency and cost.

tracking_records.title: Elastoformer: Enabling Dynamic Adaptivity via Elastic Model Transformation
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / elastic inference / pruning / runtime adaptivity
tracking_records.why: SEC 2025 framework converts pretrained ViTs and CNNs into a single elastic family that switches operating modes at runtime rather than maintaining independent models. Experiments report up to 85% FLOP reduction, 50% latency reduction, and 76% memory-overhead reduction; official author repository is public.

tracking_records.title: CLFTv2: Efficient Camera-LiDAR Fusion for Semantic Segmentation via Hierarchical Feature Pyramids
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / multimodal perception / efficient attention / edge inference
tracking_records.why: Replaces global ViT/query-matching fusion with hierarchical shifted-window attention and a lightweight FPN-style decoder. Against a Swin-based Mask2Former adaptation it uses 1.4x fewer GFLOPs and delivers 2.2x higher throughput with comparable overall accuracy while improving vulnerable-road-user recall, giving direct on-vehicle perception efficiency evidence.

tracking_records.title: AMEND: Audited Margins Enable Nonblocking Drops in GPU-PIM LLM Decoding
tracking_records.topic: KV cache/long-context / sparse attention / GPU-PIM / LLM decoding
tracking_records.why: Predicts block-sparse attention decisions from audited prior-step margins so the GPU fetches only predicted survivors while near-bank PIM concurrently checks omitted blocks, avoiding a serial selector on the token critical path. Across LongBench/RULER simulation at batch 8 it preserves near-baseline quality and reports 1.40-3.63x end-to-end decode speedup with 28-66% lower dynamic decode energy over 8K-64K contexts.

tracking_records.title: InstantMimic: A High Performance System for Learning Physics-based Skills in Seconds
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / GPU systems / robotics training
tracking_records.why: SIGGRAPH Asia 2026 system that removes fragmented-kernel and CPU-memory bottlenecks by making simulation, environment computation, policy inference, and policy updates one GPU-native execution flow. The resulting end-to-end pipeline trains diverse physics-based imitation skills in seconds and makes LLM-agent hyperparameter search practical; directly relevant to efficient Physical-AI training/runtime systems.

tracking_records.title: HBFSim: Fast and Faithful Simulation of High-Bandwidth Flash Under Real GPU Execution
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / GPU memory hierarchy / simulation / HBF
tracking_records.why: First evaluation platform applying High-Bandwidth-Flash timing, capacity, and thermal effects while a real LLM workload executes on real GPU kernels, using PTX rewriting and launch gating. It preserves unmodified vLLM/Qwen3-30B-A3B token outputs, matches all six device calibration breakpoints, and its device fast path runs the evaluated case in 2s versus 44s for the detailed reference path (20.8x), enabling practical pre-silicon memory-tier studies.

tracking_records.title: uFlowCSP: Crystal Structure Prediction using Mean flow generative models
tracking_records.topic: diffusion/flow acceleration / MeanFlow / fast generative inference
tracking_records.why: MeanFlow crystal generator completes samples in one to five network evaluations. It reports 5-58x faster inference; one step matches CrystalFlow with 100x fewer evaluations and about 10x lower wall-clock time, while five steps outperform major diffusion/flow baselines at far fewer evaluations.

tracking_records.title: Fine-Tuning a KV Cache Concatenation-Aware Model or Recomputing KV Caches? Why Not Both?
tracking_records.topic: KV cache/long-context / RAG serving / prefill acceleration
tracking_records.why: Combines KV-concatenation-aware fine-tuning with selective KV recomputation for long-context RAG. On RULER at 124k tokens it improves score by 9.7 points over recompute-only while reducing TTFT by 80% versus full attention, directly addressing the quality-efficiency tradeoff in reusable KV caches.

tracking_records.title: HiRAD: A Flexible Large-Scale AGV Routing System
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / real-time multi-agent routing / hierarchical RL / edge control
tracking_records.why: Uses hierarchical heading/velocity control and an asynchronous event-driven decision pipeline to reduce inference complexity from O(n^2) to O(n). It cuts per-step decision latency by up to 71% and reduces makespan by 45-63% on large AGV routing workloads, directly satisfying real-time Physical-AI runtime efficiency criteria.

tracking_records.title: Epoch: Compiling Diffusion Blocks for Sparse MoE Serving
tracking_records.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / diffusion language model serving / compiler-runtime
tracking_records.why: Epoch treats a diffusion-language-model block as a compilation unit, compiling active expert support and routing only live/new/refresh-required positions through fresh expert computation and expert-parallel communication. On 8 H100 GPUs across LLaDA-MoE variants from 7B to 100B, it improves end-to-end execution time by up to 2.7x over the strongest surviving baseline and remains feasible at batch sizes where baselines OOM while preserving quality.

tracking_records.title: EFQ-Softmax: Exp-Free Quantization for Softmax
tracking_records.topic: quantization / efficient attention / low-bit inference kernels
tracking_records.why: EFQ-Softmax directly generates block-scaled E2M1 probability operands from shifted attention scores, removing the high-precision exp-then-quantize path while keeping FlashAttention-style normalization and accumulation. Evaluated on Qwen3-8B, Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and WAN2.2-TI2V-5B, it preserves or improves quality and reduces fused probability-generation vector-stage latency by 40.33% on average for 16K-128K sequence lengths on the A5 vector unit.

tracking_records.title: StreamAlign: Streaming Text-Aligned Speech Tokenization
tracking_records.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / speech tokenization / streaming inference / latency
tracking_records.why: Replaces offline text-aligned speech tokenization with online RNN-T plus ASR-guided alignment and proactive word-boundary prediction. The reported tokenization latency falls from 560 ms to 270 ms while preserving recognition quality and improving downstream spoken-language modeling.

tracking_records.title: PELM: Power Efficient On-Device LLM Inference with Speculative Decoding and Dynamic Voltage Frequency Scaling
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / speculative decoding / edge inference / energy-aware runtime
tracking_records.why: PELM jointly controls DVFS, speculative decoding and variable verification depth for thermally constrained on-device LLM inference. Across hardware platforms and datasets it reports up to 23.1% speedup and 52.4% energy reduction over prior power-governing methods at comparable task quality; accepted to SenSys 2026 with an official open-source artifact.

tracking_records.title: UNISON: A Co-Designed Near-Memory Scheduler of Session KV Residency for LLM Agents
tracking_records.topic: KV cache/long-context / agent serving / near-memory scheduling
tracking_records.why: Co-designs session-level KV eviction and tiering for tool-using agent loops via a near-memory scheduler. Across 1,415 sessions and 33,596 turns, the joint policy is best non-oracle on every trace, improves hit rate by 0.3-23.1%, lowers AMAT by 22-51%, and reduces TTFT by 58-89%; the 28-nm controller is 0.169 mm^2 at 13.6 mW.

tracking_records.title: Modality-Decoupled Federated Learning for Privacy-Preserving Embodied Intelligence in 6G
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI / distributed training / edge-cloud / communication compression
tracking_records.why: IEEE Wireless Communications accepted FedMVLA decouples vision, language, and action updates for federated embodied intelligence. A 3GPP-based robotic-manipulation case study reaches 84.8% success, +22.2 points over FedAvg, scales to 128 clients across eight cells, and cuts schedule-averaged per-client uplink model-update payload by 95.6% while keeping p95 round-critical uplink completion near 1.5 s.

tracking_records.title: FPGA Acceleration of Fully Homomorphic Encryption with Adaptive Key Switching
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / privacy-preserving inference / FPGA acceleration
tracking_records.why: Co-designs a memory-efficient KLSS datapath with a runtime selector between HKS and KLSS and eliminates off-chip ciphertext transfers. On Alveo U280 it achieves 1.84-3.31x bootstrapping speedup and 1.66-2.52x secure image-classification speedup over state-of-the-art FPGA accelerators, providing strong measured accelerator evidence.

tracking_records.title: AccelMPC: High-Rate, Low-Power FPGA-Accelerated Model Predictive Control for Tiny Drones
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge robotics / FPGA acceleration / real-time control
tracking_records.why: Protected Physical-AI hardware-system co-design spanning MPC solver algorithm, numerical representation, FPGA mapping and physical integration on a 35g Crazyflie. Hardware experiments demonstrate 1 kHz onboard constrained MPC with dynamic obstacles, up to 15.6x faster solve times and 195.4x better energy-delay product than state-of-the-art embedded microcontroller solvers, scaling beyond 20,000 variables and constraints; PCB, firmware and FPGA code are open source.

tracking_records.title: Osprey: Target-agnostic Pre-training Makes Stronger Drafters in Speculative Decoding
tracking_records.topic: speculative decoding / LLM inference acceleration / drafter training
tracking_records.why: Osprey pretrains a reusable target-agnostic shallow drafter backbone and adapts it to each target with lightweight vocabulary/QKV alignment and distillation. It improves mean acceptance length by 16.1% on Qwen3-8B, 21.2% on Llama-3.3-70B-Instruct and 22.7% on MiniMax-M2.5, with 17.5% higher tokens/s on the 229B MiniMax target; accepted at EMNLP 2026 with code released.

tracking_records.title: Distributed Linear Programming on GPU Clusters at Extreme Scale
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / GPU clusters / sparse optimization / communication
tracking_records.why: 24h primary scan recovered SHARDLP, a genuinely distributed GPU solver that keeps matrix and primal-dual state sharded end to end. Eight H200 GPUs solve a 1.185B-variable/6.338B-nonzero LP in 9.9 minutes; support-aware communication cuts modelled communication by 92.97% and improves solver time by 1.27x-1.52x. This is direct measured multi-GPU systems evidence.

tracking_records.title: AuK Technical Report: An Open-Source Foundational Model for Speech Generation and Editing
tracking_records.topic: multimodal generative inference / flow distillation / low-step generation
tracking_records.why: Distills a rectified-flow speech generation/editing foundation model with consistency initialization and task-routed Decoupled DMD. AuK-Flash performs 4-step inference without classifier-free guidance and reports 4.5x wall-clock speedup over the full model under matched conditions, while retaining leading/competitive generation and editing quality.

tracking_records.title: Ostrich: Taking Large Strides Through Stiff Contact in Differentiable Dynamics
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / GPU simulation / differentiable dynamics
tracking_records.why: Ostrich is a GPU-accelerated rigid-body differentiable simulator for stiff contact that uses large timesteps, implicit differentiation and Schur-complement reuse. It reports 211x faster warm iterations than MJX, 4.7x faster than Newton Semi-Implicit, 29x checkpointed-MJX optimization throughput, and 8,192 parallel worlds on one 24GB GPU, making it strong Physical-AI simulation infrastructure.

tracking_records.title: TontaubeV1: Streaming Text-to-Speech with Hierarchical Codec Modeling and Bounded Context
tracking_records.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming speech generation / bounded-context inference / consumer GPU
tracking_records.why: 7d low-rank measured-efficiency replay recovered a direct streaming-generation systems paper absent from authority. TontaubeV1 uses hierarchical codec prediction plus bounded context to stream from a single consumer GPU; on RTX 5090 it reports about 200 ms time-to-first-audio, end-to-end RTF 0.08 for one input and aggregate RTF 0.02 across eight concurrent inputs, while releasing model weights.

tracking_records.title: HDA-MoE: Hybrid Parallelism and Dynamic, Adaptive Scheduling for Mixture-of-Experts with 3D Near-Memory Processing
tracking_records.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / 3D near-memory processing / hybrid parallelism / runtime scheduling
tracking_records.why: HDA-MoE co-designs offline hybrid TP/EP mapping and online adaptive scheduling for MoE inference on 3D near-memory processing. The primary arXiv abstract reports 1.1-3.4x speedup over TP, 1.1-1.5x over EP, 1.1-3.7x over a hybrid compute-balanced baseline, and 1.1-1.3x over HD-MoE, with source code released.

tracking_records.title: X2Streaming-ASR: wait when uncertain, emit when ready for streaming ASR
tracking_records.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / streaming ASR / realtime voice agents / low-latency inference
tracking_records.why: 7d lower-rank systematic replay recovered a direct realtime multimodal-serving paper absent from authority. X2Streaming-ASR learns when and what to commit under a single-pass hard-commit constraint; across AISHELL-1/2/3 and WenetSpeech it reports mean character-level commit latency of 27-84 ms versus 409-585 ms for evaluated streaming baselines while achieving the best streaming CER on AISHELL-1 and AISHELL-3.

tracking_records.title: Sample-Guided Exact Top-K Selection for Long-Context Sparse Attention
tracking_records.topic: efficient attention / sparse attention / GPU kernel
tracking_records.why: HPC-Ops Top-K uses fixed-stride sampling only to propose a coarse boundary while a mandatory full-row pass certifies correctness, then performs exact FP32 refinement with graph-capturable ragged dispatch. On Hy4-Preview indexer scores it beats the fastest verified exact baseline by 1.29-1.75x across 20 operator configurations (1.55x geometric mean) and gives 1.36x/1.48x on framework traces.

tracking_records.title: FlexSpIM: An Event-Based Digital Compute-In-Memory Accelerator with Flexible Operand Resolution and Layer-Wise Hybrid Stationarity
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / SNN accelerator / digital CIM
tracking_records.why: FlexSpIM is a fabricated 40-nm digital compute-in-memory SNN accelerator with bitwise operand-resolution reconfiguration and hybrid layer-wise stationarity. Prototype/system evaluation reports up to 45% energy and 52% latency reduction versus fixed-stationarity approaches while retaining 95.8% DVS gesture accuracy.

tracking_records.title: SequenceO1: End-to-End Ultra-Long (100K) Sequence Modeling in Recommendation with Low-Rank Caching
tracking_records.topic: LLM/recommendation serving / ultra-long sequence / low-rank caching / fused kernel
tracking_records.why: SequenceO1 is deployed at full traffic on Douyin for histories up to 100K interactions. Its compress-then-reason design combines target-agnostic sketches, target-conditioned cross attention, low-rank user-representation caching, multi-request batching, pipeline lift, and a fused FlashSA kernel to amortize storage, communication, and compute across online requests.

tracking_records.title: PENDA: An Efficient Processing Element via Norm-of-Difference for Deep Learning Accelerators
tracking_records.topic: AI accelerator / processing element / arithmetic architecture / energy efficiency
tracking_records.why: Exact norm-of-difference processing element uses the law of cosines to replace conventional multiply-accumulate datapaths without approximation. Reported PE-array reductions are 11-36% area, 5-48% energy, and 11-19% clock period.

tracking_records.title: FastE: Readout-Triggered Token Compression for LLM Embedding Inference
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / embedding inference / token compression / retrieval systems
tracking_records.why: Training-free readout-triggered prefix compression for Qwen3-Embedding and Qwen3-VL-Embedding. On NarrativeQA with Qwen3-Embedding-0.6B it cuts decoder-backbone FLOPs by 40.11% while retaining 99.53% of full-forward nDCG@10, with configurable quality-efficiency trade-offs across text and cross-modal retrieval tasks.

tracking_records.title: AttnCompress: Dynamic Attention-Guided Trajectory Compression for Software Engineering Agents
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / context compression / agent serving
tracking_records.why: ISSTA 2026 dynamic trajectory compression uses structure-aware segmentation, proxy-attention relevance, and a rolling recall window. On SWE-Bench-Verified and Multi-SWE-Bench it reaches 53.17% pass rate while cutting token consumption by 21.6% and total cost by 33.6%, a measured agent-serving efficiency gain without sacrificing task quality.

tracking_records.title: HoneyRoute: Honeypot-Model Routing for Adversarial LLM Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / routing / security-aware inference
tracking_records.why: HoneyRoute adds a lightweight serving router that diverts malicious requests to a honeypot model. It achieves F1=.911 with 38 ms median added latency, approximately 1/385 the latency of a two-tier guard-LLM cascade, while reducing production-model token consumption by 97.8% under adversarial flooding.

tracking_records.title: MemForest: Efficient Agent Memory Management via EventTree Partitioning and Progressive Merging
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / memory compression / retrieval
tracking_records.why: MemForest compresses continuously accumulated agent memory with event-centric partitioning, EventTree progressive merging, and anchor-guided retrieval. At 50% compression it retains 97.1% of Mem0 performance with 1.89x retrieval speedup, and 99.7% of M3-Agent performance with 2.24x retrieval speedup across robot/web multimodal benchmarks.

tracking_records.title: SemBridge: Compiling Consumer Observations into Cross-Stack Communication Plans
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / compiler / heterogeneous communication
tracking_records.why: SemBridge compiles consumer-visible distributed-tensor obligations into backend-neutral communication plans across CUDA/NCCL and CANN/HCCL. On a measured two-host 1-GbE deployment, source projection cuts result traffic by >99.97% and improves throughput by 8.92-80.20% across Dense, MoE and MiniMax workloads, providing direct systems evidence.

tracking_records.title: ActionSplice: In-Flight Action Editing for Interactive World Models
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / interactive world models / inference runtime
tracking_records.why: ActionSplice transports the interrupted backbone-native state to the revised-action state without rolling back completed solver evaluations. Across minWM-Wan Action2V and HY-WM1.5, temporal splicing provides 2.73x and 1.69x pixel-ready speedups over waiting while substantially reducing rollback-relative perceptual error.

tracking_records.title: GPU-Enabled Large-Scale Optimization Using Randomized Linear Algebra
tracking_records.topic: GPU kernel/DSL/compilers / scientific ML / randomized linear algebra
tracking_records.why: rlaopt is an Apache-licensed PyTorch package that exposes GPU-enabled randomized-linear-algebra solvers for positive-definite systems and constrained convex empirical-risk problems, including NystromPCG, NysADMM and SAPPHIRE. The primary abstract reports substantial GPU-execution speedups across ridge regression, bounded multinomial logistic regression and bounded elastic net, while also supporting differentiation through solver iterations, making this a practical reusable GPU systems/runtime contribution.

tracking_records.title: mjorbit: A Simulation Framework for Space Robotics
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / robotics runtime / GPU simulation
tracking_records.why: mjorbit extends MuJoCo with spacecraft dynamics, actuators and sensors and exposes both low-latency C++ CPU and high-throughput GPU backends for contact-rich space robotics. It demonstrates realistic on-orbit MPC and RL case studies and provides open-source code, making it a concrete Physical-AI runtime/simulation infrastructure contribution.

tracking_records.title: Deadline-Aware Adaptive Prefill Chunking for Efficient Large Language Model Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / chunked prefill / SLO scheduling / goodput
tracking_records.why: SLOWeave chooses the largest prefill chunk predicted to complete before the earliest active decode deadline. GPU-runtime evaluation reports 39% and 38% goodput gains over the strongest fixed-chunk baseline on mixed and long-context workloads at 25 ms TPOT, rising to 3.3x and 2.4x under a 10 ms objective.

tracking_records.title: ComVLA: Communication-Aware Split Inference for VLA Models in 6G-Connected Robotics
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / split inference / cloud-edge robotics / wireless-aware token budgeting
tracking_records.why: ComVLA adapts the transmitted visual-token budget to wireless channel capacity for cloud-offloaded VLA inference. On LIBERO, sending 32 instead of 512 tokens cuts inference compute by 74% and inference latency by 22% versus OpenVLA-OFT, with 95.4% versus 96.9% average task success, and the paper is accepted to IEEE GLOBECOM 2026.

tracking_records.title: A*-Thought-V2: Efficient Latent Reasoning via Geometric Dynamics of LLM
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / latent reasoning / token compression / efficient training
tracking_records.why: Interleaves explicit text with pooled continuous latent tokens using geometric trajectory alignment. Across Qwen3.5-9B and Qwen3.6-27B it improves average accuracy by up to 2.6% while cutting response length by up to half, raising Accuracy per Computation Unit by 2.29x, and reducing preprocessing/training time by 94.6%/up to 80.3%.

tracking_records.title: Scalability Analysis of Distributed Kolmogorov-Arnold Network Training on High-Performance Computing Systems
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / multi-GPU scaling / HPC / DDP
tracking_records.why: 7d lower-rank replay recovered a direct empirical multi-node multi-GPU scaling study. KAN data-parallel training reaches 5.97x speedup and 74.7% parallel efficiency at 8 NVIDIA A100 GPUs across 4 nodes, with communication overhead characterized at 1.3%-6.1%. This is concrete distributed-training systems evidence rather than only an algorithmic KAN paper.

tracking_records.title: TFTrack: A Template-Free Framework for Efficient 3D Point Cloud Tracking
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / efficient perception / 3D tracking
tracking_records.why: TFTrack removes redundant template-search pair processing and complex motion modeling from 3D single-object tracking. On KITTI and nuScenes it remains competitive while reducing FLOPs by about 50% and running at about 120 FPS, directly supporting real-time robotic perception.

tracking_records.title: GPU-Accelerated Hypergraph Partitioning and Placement to Map SNNs on Neuromorphic Hardware
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / neuromorphic accelerator / GPU compiler-mapping
tracking_records.why: This work builds a GPU-accelerated hypergraph partitioning and placement pipeline for mapping million-neuron SNNs to neuromorphic cores. The mapper is 18-280x faster on average than sequential tools while model-based evaluation reports up to 16% lower communication latency and 42% lower spike-movement energy.

tracking_records.title: Analytical Resource Management for Fine-grained MoE Computation-Communication Overlap
tracking_records.topic: MoE systems/accelerators / distributed inference / compute-communication overlap
tracking_records.why: A wave-quantized analytical model selects communication CTA count and SM-resource partition before launch for dependency-coupled MoE overlap. Integrated into COMET/FLUX on four A100 GPUs, it reports 2.528x geometric-mean speedup at GEMM2+GatherRS, 1.771x at the post-router MoE layer, and 1.185x complete-model prefill versus COMET, with 0.157 us mean solver overhead.

tracking_records.title: TASTE: Throughput-Aware Batch Size Tuning for On-Device Edge Learning
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / on-device learning / throughput tuning
tracking_records.why: Bayesian-optimization-based batch-size tuning for on-device training explicitly targets hardware throughput ceilings across edge devices. With gradient accumulation and linear learning-rate scaling, the paper reports up to 2x training-throughput improvement on Raspberry Pi 4 versus maximum-batch-size settings without accuracy loss.

tracking_records.title: RAFM-SER++: A Lightweight Multimodal Emotion Recognition Framework for Real-Time Behavioral Monitoring in Surveillance Systems
tracking_records.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / lightweight asymmetric fusion / real-time inference
tracking_records.why: Replaces interaction-heavy bidirectional multimodal fusion with one-directional residual attention. Reports >60% fewer trainable parameters, 79.60 it/s inference, and strong BACC on IEMOCAP/ESD; direct measured accuracy-efficiency evidence.

tracking_records.title: Federated Binary Gating with Server-Side Vision-Language Inference for Surveillance Anomaly Classification
tracking_records.topic: multimodal/MLLM serving / edge-cloud gating / selective VLM inference / federated systems
tracking_records.why: Uses a lightweight federated local video gate so only flagged clips invoke server-side Qwen3-VL-8B. In a real three-node heterogeneous deployment, fixed-threshold routing preserves nearly the same macro-F1 as centralized CNN+VLM while transmitting only 51.4% of videos, providing measured selective-offload and server-VLM utilization reduction.

tracking_records.title: Fast simulation of nonlinear deep resistive networks for energy-based computation
tracking_records.topic: AI accelerator / analog computing / simulator acceleration / energy-based computation
tracking_records.why: Extends coordinate-descent circuit simulation from ideal diodes to realistic monotone nonlinear devices. Across deep resistive networks it matches SPICE steady states with very low error while reaching speedups up to 1.7e3x; MNIST training on a 1568x100x20 double-Shockley network cuts per-epoch time by roughly 4.4e2x.

tracking_records.title: PV-WM: A Heterogeneous Micro-Macro World Model for Articulated Pedestrian-Vehicle Co-Rollout
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / world model / efficient rollout
tracking_records.why: PV-WM jointly rolls out articulated pedestrians and vehicles with a single recurrent model. Relative to a modular specialist it uses 57.1% fewer parameters, 96.5% lower average FLOPs per local scene and 25.5% lower measured p95 latency while improving forecast errors, giving direct efficient world-model evidence.

tracking_records.title: An Efficient Out-of-Core Tomographic Imaging Framework for Edge Devices
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / GPU kernel / mixed precision / out-of-core
tracking_records.why: edgeFBP is an end-to-end out-of-core CT reconstruction runtime for Nvidia Jetson SoCs using mixed precision and Tensor Cores for the bottleneck back-projection kernel. It reports 1.83x speedup over RTK on Jetson Nano, 2.56x on Jetson AGX, and up to 5-48x higher energy efficiency than DGX A100 under a 25W budget, giving direct measured edge-system evidence.

tracking_records.title: CEDAR: Error-Bounded Residual Routing for Efficient Long-Context Attention
tracking_records.topic: efficient attention / long context / sparse routing / kernel acceleration
tracking_records.why: CEDAR combines chunk summaries with error-aware exact refinement instead of hard-dropping omitted chunks, preserving global coverage with a variable refinement budget. The primary abstract reports over 98% reconstruction-error reduction versus hard dropping at equal exact-chunk budgets and approximately 3x kernel speedup at 128K context.

tracking_records.title: Parallelism Strategy Chaining for Fast Training Convergence
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / parallelism / online adaptation
tracking_records.why: CONA observes that the best data/tensor/pipeline strategy changes during training and switches strategies online using a throughput-and-gradient surrogate. Across GPT-3 1.3B, BERT-Large and Llama-3.2-1B it reaches target perplexity 1.4-9.6x faster than prior strategy-selection methods.

tracking_records.title: Agentic Algorithm Engineering: Improving Shared-Memory Exact Minimum Cuts
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / autonomous algorithm engineering / shared-memory optimization / performance tuning
tracking_records.why: Autonomous LLM agents repeatedly profile, modify and benchmark an already heavily hand-tuned shared-memory exact minimum-cut implementation. The resulting changes yield 1.28x sequential and 1.63x 32-thread speedups on real-world k-cores, and 6.26x/127x on DIMACS core instances, providing direct measured evidence that agentic systems can improve low-level algorithm/runtime efficiency rather than only generate code.

tracking_records.title: Enabling High-Bandwidth Flash for Generative Recommendation Serving with Write-Aware KV Cache Policy
tracking_records.topic: LLM/recommendation serving / KV cache / flash tiering / endurance-aware cache policy
tracking_records.why: The work studies HBF-backed user-level KV reuse for generative recommendation and introduces admission-controlled write-aware LRU-K. Primary results report 3.8-4.7x throughput over HBM-only systems while extending modeled HBF lifetime from about one year to over six years at K=10 with comparable throughput.

tracking_records.title: Online Draft Co-Training for Speculative Decoding in Large-Scale, Long-Context RL Post-Training
tracking_records.topic: speculative decoding / RL post-training / context parallelism / pipeline parallelism
tracking_records.why: The system co-trains speculative drafts during large-scale RL rollout generation, extending packed zigzag-ring context parallelism with branch attention and adding TapChannel to move target features across pipeline stages without disturbing the pipeline schedule. It reports substantial rollout and end-to-end speedups up to 122B models, strong scaling to 256K context, memory savings, and modest PP transport overhead.

tracking_records.title: ASTRA: Low-Overhead Runtime Architecture for STReam Adaptation in Video Analytics
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / multimodal serving / runtime adaptation
tracking_records.why: ASTRA is a low-overhead runtime for online resolution/frame-rate adaptation in live edge video analytics, deployed on the NSF COSMOS testbed and evaluated with up to eight cameras under real network conditions. It maintains over 90% probability of meeting accuracy/latency requirements, stays within 10% of offline-optimal performance, and adds about 2% average GPU-utilization overhead per camera.

tracking_records.title: RedKnot-MLA: Multi-Head Offline-Online Reuse for DeepSeek-V4 Long-Context Serving
tracking_records.topic: LLM serving / KV cache reuse / MLA / long context
tracking_records.why: RedKnot-MLA adapts head-aware offline-online reuse to packed MLA without splitting the latent KV stream. Frozen operating points report 2.02-3.84x hot-artifact TTFT speedups and about 2.0x preliminary 256K QPS, with 78.7-79.5% analytic major-operator arithmetic saving at 256K.

tracking_records.title: TreeRedux: Separating Concerns in Spark's Distributed Tree Aggregation
tracking_records.topic: distributed training/inference / data systems / runtime memory scalability
tracking_records.why: Minimal Spark tree-aggregation extension that executes a terminal finalize step on an executor so compact result V rather than large intermediate U is materialized on the driver. Default GK Select OOMs at 2.5B elements and executor-side final aggregation at about 16-18B, while Redux Select completes through 28B; Space-Saving supports up to 32x larger sketch capacity. Strong measured distributed-runtime scalability evidence.

tracking_records.title: OCTN: Neural OCT Representations for Robot-Guided Precision Intervention
tracking_records.topic: VLA/WAM/Physical AI serving / edge/GPU runtime / robot-guided intervention
tracking_records.why: OCTN stores a continuous OCT tissue representation natively on GPU for fast geometric reasoning and robot integration. It reports up to 43x faster intensity-based spatial queries than conventional CPU processing, 4x lower acquisition time from sparse B-scans, sub-10s training, and demonstrates OCT-guided robotic laser surgery, making it strong protected Physical-AI runtime evidence.

tracking_records.title: Uni-Light: An Ultra-Lightweight Framework via Uncertainty-Aware Knowledge Distillation for Brain Tumour Segmentation
tracking_records.topic: edge/cloud/heterogeneous AI systems / lightweight neural networks / knowledge distillation / memory-FLOP efficiency
tracking_records.why: Targets deployment efficiency directly: the ultra-lightweight 3D segmentation model reduces parameters by 97.56%, FLOPs by 73.03%, and inference memory footprint by 81.58% while retaining or improving segmentation fidelity on BraTS2023-GLI and MSD-BTS. These are explicit multi-axis inference-efficiency gains, so it clears the strong quality gate despite the medical application domain.

tracking_records.title: RoLA: Rotary-Positioned Low-Rank Linear Attention for Efficient Diffusion Transformers
tracking_records.topic: video/image generation acceleration / diffusion/flow acceleration / efficient attention
tracking_records.why: RoLA places RoPE outside a nonlinear low-rank feature map so the global branch keeps a reusable linear summary while preserving relative rotary geometry. On Wan2.1-14B video generation at 720p/81 frames on H100, the sparse-low-rank module remains competitive at 90% sparsity and achieves 2.63x measured end-to-end inference speedup.

tracking_records.title: PARSER: Read in Parallel, Reason in Depth for Long-Context LLM Agents
tracking_records.topic: efficient reasoning/agent systems / long-context / parallel inference
tracking_records.why: PARSER decouples document reading from reasoning using frozen chunk-local subagents and iterative scatter-gather lead-agent reasoning. On 7K-896K-token multi-hop QA it improves quality while reducing inference latency by up to 11x versus sequential memory agents, making it a strong efficient-agent inference result.

tracking_records.title: TileMix: Tile-Centric Mixed-Precision Attention for LLM Inference Acceleration
tracking_records.topic: mixed-precision attention kernel / long-context inference
tracking_records.why: Long-context prefill in large language models (LLMs) incurs substantial computation and memory traffic because dense self-attention computes quadratic query-key scores. Existing methods either use a uniform low-precision path or select token interactions, leaving spatial precision routing over hardware-aligned score tiles outside fused dense attention. We introduce TileMix, a tile-centric precision-routing kernel that makes numerical precision an executable spatial decision over score-tile groups within fused dense attention. TileMix partitions the attention matrix into hardware-aligned score tiles, packs routing decisions into compact bitmasks, and dispatches each tile group through FP16 or INT8 score computation while both paths update a shared online-softmax state. Scalable precision grouping lets each routing bit govern multiple adjacent key tiles, preserving hardware-aligned compute tiles and compact metadata at long contexts. By routing all legal tile groups, TileMix preserves dense token connectivity, requires no training, and supports grouped-query attention, variable-length batches, and INT8 key/value caches. Across LongEval, LV-Eval, and A100 prefill benchmarks on LLaMA, Qwen, and Vicuna, TileMix recovers long-context quality lost under uniform INT8 and improves prefill throughput over FP16, yielding a controllable accuracy-efficiency frontier across model families. The implementation is available at https://github.com/HanzhiZhang-Ulrica/TileMix.

tracking_records.title: TEMPO: Makespan-Aware Expert-Parallel Load Balancing Across Memory- and Compute-Bound Regimes
tracking_records.topic: MoE expert-parallel load balancing / serving
tracking_records.why: In expert-parallel (EP) MoE serving, every layer synchronizes at the slowest GPU. Dispatchers balance token counts (EPLB, LPLB, UltraEP) or activated-expert counts (METRO), assuming expert time is linear in one. Measurements on two datacenter GPU generations show it is neither: below $n^* \approx 156$--$168$ tokens, HBM weight streaming dominates---cost attaches to $activated replicas$, not tokens; above it, grouped GEMM rounds tokens to 128-tile $M$-tiles, so $splitting$ an expert adds padded compute. A max-affine profile $t=\max(a+bG,\,c+βN)$ captures both regimes. Realistic decode batches hold hot experts in the linear regime and cold in the flat $simultaneously$; recorded batches show proxy dispatches differ by $1.4$--$1.6\times$ in modeled block time (p95 up to $1.7\times$), and $which$ proxy wins flips with the regime. We formalize per-batch dispatch as a fixed-charge makespan problem---NP-hard on two fully replicated GPUs, polynomial in degenerate limits---and present TEMPO, a makespan-aware dispatcher solving it in milliseconds off the critical path; its SGLang integration runs out-of-process and fuses dispatch with count collection into one in-graph kernel. Anchored by an 8-GPU Testbed A microbenchmark, TEMPO stays within $1\%$ of the best fixed baseline everywhere and wins by up to $15.5\%$ where regimes mix. End-to-end on Testbed B, Qwen3-235B (inside the win region) gains $4$--$6\%$ throughput and cuts p99 latency by $\sim 15.6\%$; DeepSeek-V3 (outside, communication-dominated) shows only mechanism cost. A phase diagram, not a universal win, is the claim: it predicts both outcomes before deployment.

tracking_records.title: SCOPE: Subspace Clustering with Online Per-Head Top-K Estimation for Sparse Video Attention
tracking_records.topic: sparse video attention / DiT inference
tracking_records.why: Diffusion Transformers (DiTs) incur quadratic self-attention cost over spatiotemporal tokens. Existing training-free sparse attention methods often construct sparse masks from block-level or cluster-level proxy scores, which can obscure fine-grained differences among keys and miss high contribution keys under aggressive sparsity. Moreover, such proxy scores may yield overly concentrated softmax distributions, causing Top-$p$ to retain too few keys for some query clusters. Although a fixed Top-$k$ minimum alleviates this failure mode, a shared value cannot adapt to variations across heads and inputs. To address both limitations, we propose SCOPE, a training-free sparse attention framework that combines 3D-RoPE-aligned key subspace clustering with online per-head Top-$k$ estimation for efficient video-DiT inference. SCOPE partitions post-RoPE keys into temporal, height, and width subspaces, clusters them independently, and aggregates the corresponding centroid scores through lookup tables to obtain per key proxy scores for each query cluster. Building on existing hybrid Top-$p$/fixed Top-$k$ selection, SCOPE derives a head-specific Top-$k$ value online by averaging the initial retained key counts within each head, weighted by query cluster size, and selects additional keys only for query clusters whose initial retained key counts fall below this value. Sparse attention is then computed over the selected original keys and values. Across six model--task configurations, SCOPE consistently outperforms existing training-free baselines in both fidelity and latency, achieving up to a $1.99\times$ end-to-end speedup on 720p HunyuanVideo with $28.46$ dB PSNR relative to dense attention.

tracking_records.title: GraniKV: Asymmetric Granularity KV-Cache Paging for Multi-Agent Systems with Long Shared Prefix
tracking_records.topic: KV-cache paging / multi-agent serving
tracking_records.why: Production paged-serving engines apply uniform paging granularity to the KV cache, even though the two regions of a multi-agent workload have opposite storage requirements: a long shared prefix demands contiguity, while the per-request suffix demands fine-grained allocation. We present \textbf{GraniKV}, a KV-cache layer that allocates the shared prefix in a contiguous HOT pool and the suffix in a token-level COLD pool, combined with a per-step dispatcher which selects the appropriate backend among dual backends for each regime (compute-, memory-, or communication-bound). To the best of our knowledge, GraniKV is the first system to apply asymmetric paging granularity to the KV cache of a production paged-serving engine. At $L_p{=}16$\,K shared tokens GraniKV reaches $\mathbf{2.16\times}$, $\mathbf{1.98\times}$, and $\mathbf{1.57\times}$ output-token throughput over the production baseline on Llama-3.1-8B/TP=1, Qwen-2.5-14B/TP=2, and Qwen-2.5-32B/TP=4. The gain decomposes: cascade attention integration contributes the majority at saturation; the asymmetric storage layer adds $1.05$--$1.15\times$ end-to-end while being what makes the batched-GEMM prefix backend possible at all. Under heterogeneous multi-agent serving with \emph{distinct} prompts of different lengths, the attribution inverts: GraniKV sustains $\mathbf{1.95\times}$ while batch-global cascade collapses to parity --- the storage layer alone carries the win in the regime that motivates the paper.

tracking_records.title: Global Simulation-Guided Dynamic Operator Scheduling for Efficient Multi-Tenant Model Serving
tracking_records.topic: multi-tenant model serving / operator-level scheduling
tracking_records.why: Container-granularity scheduling leaves abundant short-lived idle slices within containers unexploited. Reallocating containers is too heavyweight to utilize such fine-grained opportunities under SLA constraints, and operator-level scheduling requires reasoning about dependencies, memory safety, and cluster-wide execution dynamics in real time. In this paper, we present SliceScheduler, a dynamic operator-level scheduling system for multi-tenant model serving. The key idea is to expose cluster-wide operator execution state and enable what-if reasoning over scheduling decisions. SliceScheduler consists of four key components. First, we introduce the Global Mapping Graph (GMG), a unified abstraction that captures operator dependencies, tensor shapes, resource mappings, and execution states, providing a real-time, cluster-wide view with explicit resource semantics. Second, we build a global simulator on top of GMG to predict operator-level execution and memory evolution under candidate placements. Third, we design an incremental, simulation-based scheduling module that selects placements to exploit fragmented idle slices while avoiding memory violations and preserving SLA. Finally, we develop an operator executor that materializes scheduling decisions on GPUs and coordinates computation and cross-accelerator transfers. We implement SliceScheduler as a PyTorch backend and evaluate it using production trace replay. Experimental results show that SliceScheduler improves token throughput by 1.10--2.29$\times$ compared to existing approaches, while maintaining SLA violations within 9\%. SliceScheduler demonstrates that operator-level scheduling is a practical and effective approach to improving GPU utilization for multi-tenant LLM serving.

tracking_records.title: From Local Mismatch to Global Impact: Optimizing Cache Reuse Policy for Efficient Diffusion
tracking_records.topic: diffusion cache policy / video-image generation acceleration
tracking_records.why: Diffusion models have achieved dominant performance in visual generation but suffer from substantial inference overhead. While cache-based acceleration has emerged as a promising solution, existing policies rely on local similarity heuristics, which we identify as being significantly misaligned with final generation quality. This discrepancy stems from the non-uniform propagation and accumulation of errors along the denoising trajectory. To address this, we propose Global-Impact Cache (GCache). We first establish a rigorous theoretical characterization of the error propagation upper bound. Recognizing that this bound can be overly conservative for complex, highly non-convex diffusion models, we further reparameterize the propagation exponent with a Bernstein form and reformulate cache policy search as a bilevel optimization problem. In detail, GCache identifies an optimal reuse policy in the inner objective while aligning the error-weighting function with generation quality loss in the outer objective. This framework effectively reconciles theoretical rigor with empirical performance, learning to prioritize computation where it most impacts visual fidelity. Extensive experiments demonstrate that GCache consistently outperforms prior caching strategies on both video and image generation. Notably, on the state-of-the-art Wan2.1 video diffusion model, GCache maintains a 2.17x speedup while significantly enhancing generation quality, reducing LPIPS from 0.1095 to 0.0316.

tracking_records.title: From LLM Inference to Agentic Workloads: Characterization and Implications for Serving Systems
tracking_records.topic: agentic serving characterization / systems benchmark
tracking_records.why: Agentic applications are shifting AI serving from isolated model inference to long-running workloads in which LLMs coordinate tools, environments, and persistent state. However, the system behavior of these workloads---where latency, cost, and bottlenecks arise---remains poorly characterized, leaving serving systems to rely on assumptions built for conventional inference. We present AgentSysBench, a benchmark suite and measurement toolkit with ten representative agentic applications and unified systems-level instrumentation. Across controlled deployments and production traces, we identify six properties that distinguish agentic workloads from conventional LLM serving: (1) execution is heavyweight and stateful, with non-LLM components dominating latency in 5 of 10 applications and sandbox working-set memory peaking at 28 GB per session; (2) applications compose components with heterogeneous resource affinity---GPU-bound inference, memory-bound retrieval, CPU-bound sandboxes---whose task latencies diverge by up to 32x; (3) bottlenecks shift across requests, models, and deployments; (4) production sessions hold state idle for minutes to hours between active steps; (5) a control-plane tax---auxiliary LLM calls and context overhead from tool schemas and observations---crowds out productive compute and context; and (6) production traces from three applications reveal heavy cross-request redundancy in search queries and web fetches, exposing a large caching opportunity. Four design explorations demonstrate that these findings are actionable: task-aware serving reduces latency by 29--40%, communication-aware placement by up to 4.5x, state offloading reduces memory usage by 4.6x, and tool-result caching removes 35.2% of redundant search calls and saves 19.3% of aggregate search latency.

tracking_records.title: Every Expert Counts: ExactMoE for Memory-Efficient W4A16 Inference
tracking_records.topic: MoE memory-efficient W4A16 inference / GPU slot cache
tracking_records.why: Sparse mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models reduce arithmetic by activating only a small subset of experts per token, yet deployment still requires storing and moving the full expert bank. We present ExactMoE, an inference design that applies symmetric group-128 four-bit weight quantization only to routed experts, stores those experts in kernel-native MARLIN form in pinned host memory, and executes all selected experts through a configurable GPU-resident slot cache and fused grouped MoE kernels. The router, attention, embeddings, normalization layers, and language-model head remain in BF16. "Exact" refers to complete expert availability and an unchanged top-k routing procedure: no expert is pruned, substituted, or forced to execute on the CPU. It does not imply numerical identity with the BF16 model. On OLMoE-1B-7B-0924-Instruct, evaluated on a single NVIDIA L4, a 16-slot configuration reduces peak reserved GPU memory from 14.168 to 1.836 GiB (87.04%) while retaining 81.85% of BF16 decode throughput. A fully resident 64-slot configuration reaches 31.923 tokens/s versus 21.662 tokens/s for BF16 while reserving 4.061 GiB. Across 12,450 zero-shot multiple-choice questions, ExactMoE obtains 70.3534% normalized accuracy versus 70.8996% for BF16, retaining 99.23% of the baseline accuracy. In a matched 16-token ablation, fused grouped execution is 1.97x as fast as a sequential W4 reference. These results identify a practical memory-transfer-throughput frontier for complete-expert MoE inference.

tracking_records.title: EcoVLA: Energy-Efficient Device-Edge Co-Inference for Vision-Language-Action Models under Real-Time Constraints
tracking_records.topic: VLA device-edge co-inference / energy-aware runtime
tracking_records.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have emerged as a promising foundation for Embodied AI, but their high inference cost poses significant challenges for deployment in robotic systems. In practice, on-device inference is constrained by limited compute capacity and energy budgets, struggling to simultaneously satisfy real-time control and energy efficiency requirements. Alternatively, offloading the inference workload to an edge server is susceptible to fluctuations in system conditions, introducing unpredictable latency risks. Device-edge co-inference offers a promising solution, but systematic research tailored to VLA models remains scarce, particularly a unified co-inference framework that jointly addresses real-time constraints and system-level energy efficiency. Thus, we propose EcoVLA, an adaptive device-edge co-inference framework for VLA models that maximizes system energy efficiency under real-time constraints. EcoVLA first introduces a unified stage-level abstraction over different VLA paradigms, establishing an architecture-agnostic co-inference design space. It then formulates a joint device-edge-network latency and energy prediction model to enable rapid runtime evaluation of candidate co-inference schemes. Building on this, EcoVLA continuously selects the energy-optimal scheme satisfying real-time constraints with millisecond-level overhead, adapting to runtime variations in network and system states. Furthermore, EcoVLA incorporates a lightweight transmission mechanism for inter-stage intermediate tensors to reduce the communication overhead incurred by cross-device collaboration. Experimental results across VLA models show that EcoVLA improves system energy efficiency by up to 236% over existing co-inference approaches under a 20 Hz action output frequency constraint, while consistently maintaining SLO satisfaction under dynamic network and edge workload conditions.

tracking_records.title: DeaMoE: Efficient MoE Structure for Fast Small-Batch Decoding
tracking_records.topic: MoE architecture / small-batch decoding
tracking_records.why: Mixture-of-Experts (MoE) models have been widely adopted in real-time interactive applications such as coding assistants, real-time audio-video interaction systems. To meet the extremely low response latency requirements of these scenarios, practitioners commonly employ small-batch decoding, under which MoE inference becomes memory-bound and is severely bottlenecked by expert weight loading. However, this bottleneck has received limited attention, and existing solutions such as post-training weight compression or fine-grained expert design during pre-training either degrade model accuracy or introduce additional computation and communication overhead. To tackle this issue, we propose DeaMoE, a decoding-efficient MoE architecture, in which the experts are grouped into several departments, and the experts belonging to the same department share most parameters since they come from the same professional field, and additionally each expert contains a few private parameters to reflect its uniqueness. Moreover, we design customized two-stage routing strategy for DeaMoE to avoid redundant loading, under which DeaMoE greatly improves the efficiency during LLM decoding. Compared with vanilla MoE, DeaMoE reduces per-step loaded weights by up to 50.9% and achieves up to 1.33 end-to-end TPOT speedup for the pre-trained 7B model on A40, and up to 2.00x and 1.97x peak speedup for DeepSeek-V3 on A40 and H100 in microbenchmarks.

tracking_records.title: Beyond Capacity: Scalable MoE LLM Inference via High-Bandwidth Flash with Direct GPU and HBM Paths
tracking_records.topic: MoE serving / high-bandwidth flash architecture
tracking_records.why: Modern mixture-of-experts (MoE) language models increasingly strain the capacity and cost efficiency of high-bandwidth memory (HBM), as rapidly growing expert weights must be provisioned close to GPUs. High-bandwidth flash (HBF) offers substantially greater capacity, but conventional designs typically deliver HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through HBM, leaving an additional direct GPU-HBF connection underutilized. We explore an HBF organization that simultaneously exploits two independent expert-delivery routes: a direct path that transfers expert weights from HBF to the GPU and a relay path that transfers them from HBF through the HBM base die to the GPU. Whole experts are assigned to one of the two routes, and transfers over both routes proceed concurrently, increasing aggregate expert-delivery bandwidth without replicating expert weights or introducing a shared relay bottleneck. Early expert determination identifies upcoming experts ahead of their conventional execution point, allowing HBF read latency to overlap with preceding computation, while separate management of immutable expert weights and mutable KV-cache data reduces interference between the two traffic classes. We evaluate the architecture using an event-driven continuous-batching LLM serving simulator with empirically measured GPU compute latencies. Across representative MoE workloads, concurrently utilizing the direct GPU-HBF and HBF-HBM-GPU routes consistently improves expert-delivery efficiency over designs restricted to either route alone. For a representative workload, the proposed architecture can achieve 1.94$\times$ higher throughput and 1.90$\times$ end-to-end speedup over a design that delivers all HBF-resident expert weights to the GPU through the HBM base die.

tracking_records.title: Algorithm-Architecture Co-Design for Efficient VLA Inference via Speculative Inference and Verification
tracking_records.topic: VLA speculative inference / algorithm-architecture co-design
tracking_records.why: Vision-Language-Action (VLA) models have demonstrated remarkable capabilities in the field of embodied AI, but their high computational cost and limited predicted action length hinder real-time deployment. Although Dadu-Corki, a dedicated accelerator for efficient embodied AI, has been introduced, it does not exploit the inherent interaction patterns between the robot and its environment, which results in a relatively short predicted action length. We observe that robotic environments naturally alternate between active states-where precise actions are crucial-and inactive states-where actions have limited impact on task success. This insight enables a new scheduling opportunity: long-action-length speculative prediction in inactive states, paired with selective verification in active states. We propose SpecVLA, an algorithm-system co-design framework that adaptively balances action length, inference latency, and task reliability. On the algorithm side, SpecVLA introduces a state-aware VLA inference execution paradigm and a hardware-friendly construction of a smaller verification model (sVLA) using differential residuals and block-wise mixed-precision quantization. On the system side, we develop a heterogeneous architecture consisting of a GPU and a robotic-specific hardware module, along with a speculative dataflow that decouples VLA and sVLA through parallel execution. Comprehensive evaluations on OpenVLA and RDT across LIBERO and ManiSkill benchmarks show that SpecVLA reduces end-to-end latency significantly while preserving task success rate. By enabling long-action-length speculative prediction with timely verification, SpecVLA achieves real-time robotic manipulation with both high efficiency and reliability.
